AboutKind.description: The kind of subject a topic can be about.

oneOf.description:
The whole jurisdiction the conversation is in (the town; a region or
the nation where the player and the speaker are at that tier): its
worries, as a whole (DEC-098).

ActDef.description:
One act of a career: every post of a tier (less `except`), or the named
posts.

except.description: Posts of `tier` that belong to a later act (body or office ids).

posts.description: The act's posts (body or office ids), when it is not a whole tier.

ActFlowParams.description:
The act flow (DEC-005, DEC-012): directives, interrupts, skip targets,
the proxy and the Legacy record.

ActionParams.description:
Player action effects and risks (DEC-073). Time and health costs are in
`tuning.action_costs`; record gains in `career.record_gain`.

late_night_health.description: Health a late-night action costs on top of its own cost.

talks.description:
Fundraising, the press, the bribe and the leak as conversations
(DEC-114, B5): whom each is had with and what they say.

visit.description: The `visit` action: its verbs and numbers (places with purpose).

AiInput.description: Normalised (0..1) inputs the engine computes for an NPC each decision.

oneOf.description: 1 while the NPC is a candidate in an open race.
0 at the start of the campaign, 1 on election eve.
1 for a dead heat (from polls when published, else party strength).
1 − the NPC's mean awareness among the race's voters.
Campaign funds relative to a few weeks of advertising.
Strength of the NPC's view on the most important pending bill.
1 when that bill's vote is on a knife edge.
Appeal of the NPC's best policy idea (own values and constituents).
1 if the NPC has no bill of their own pending.
1 when the council has few bills pending.
Always 1.

top_n.description: Choose by weighted chance among the best `top_n` scores.

AmbientParams.description: Ambient people: generated on demand at places, never stored (DEC-018).

max_listed.description: Most people listed at a place, Named and Ambient together.

period_days.description: Who is around changes every this many days.

present.description: People present at a public place, [min, max].

sway_keep.description: Share of the goodwill already built on a bill that survives an amendment.

ArcBeat.description:
Something a stage offers. `ArcBeat`, because `narrative::BeatDef` is a
scene's spoken line.

oneOf.description:
A dilemma with the arc's cast (roles of the same ids). `on`: what
each option does to the run; a default at the deadline counts.

An ask (`from: ["arc"]`) from a cast person; the beat is done when
it is kept.
The arc's own choice in a conversation with a cast person.
Something to do at a cast place or in a cast area.

verb_key.description: The button (no arguments: the place lists it).

oneOf.description: A story the outlets may run.

An overheard line that holds while the stage does (its own
conditions name the arc).

A cast person acts: a keyed weekly draw at `weight`, scaled by
their boldness.

line_key.description: How Today and the skip summary report it.

oneOf.description:
A played scene of a few rounds (DEC-112; [`crate::exchange`]): the
other side puts true things to the player, who answers with lines
they have earned, before an audience bound from live state.

at.description: Where it is held: a place role.

audience.description: One to five groups in all.

outcome.description: What each end state does to the run (marks, heat, gated effects).

params.description:
Constants this scene sets for itself: dotted paths into
[`ExchangeParams`] (`"win": 0.1`, `"cover.own": 0.5`).

text.description: The key prefix of its sentences (`exchange-debate`).

time.description: What taking part costs, for the whole scene.

once.description: Done at most once in a run (default).

sets.description: A mark set when it is done.

teaches.description: What doing it teaches about the arc (task A3).

when.description: Offered while these hold (the run's marks, heat and days; state).

ArcCast.description: How a role binds to something real, relative to the arc's jurisdiction.

oneOf.description:
A named person there with one of these occupations (in list order,
then the most influential); with `near`, one who lives in that area
role first.

at.description:
With `at`, one whose own workplace is the place cast in that
role first (a plant's steward and its manager), before `near`.

oneOf.description:
A named plant there (DEC-110) in one of these states (none given:
any open one): the most advanced in its review first (under notice,
then on short time, then running), then the most jobs, then the
lowest id. Bound to the plant's place.

Whoever holds a post there whose constitution lists this power (not
the player; an office before a seat). `party` is a preference,
never a filter: one of the player's party first (`same`: whoever
thinks most of the player), or of another first (`other`: whoever
thinks least), then anyone else who holds the power.
The player's named rival there (a town's; local-only).
Someone there the player owes a favour (the largest debt).
An area one level down: of a town, a neighbourhood.

place.description:
With `place`, the area that holds the place cast in that earlier
role comes first (a plant's own district), then `pick`.

oneOf.description:
An open place of one of these kinds (in list order); with `near`,
one in that area role first.

Where the person cast in `of` works: the place their post sits (the
constitution's `works_at`), else their own workplace.
Another jurisdiction.
What raised the arc (a plant, a fact). Not yet: task A5.

ArcChoiceDef.description:
The arc's own choice in a conversation with a cast person (a talk
hook): the button, what the player says, and the replies, the first
whose conditions hold being said. The last has no conditions.

answers.description: Policy templates NPC agendas favour while it runs (task A2).

cooldown_days.description: Days before it may be raised again in the same jurisdiction.

facts.description:
Readings for the text: conditions evaluated for their arguments
only (one without bounds always holds), with the arc's roles.

frame.description:
How the player arrives into it as an opening the draft offers
(DEC-101 §2, STAGED_ARCS §6.6; task A8). Without one the arc is
never offered as an opening.

given.description:
Conditions on the cast as bound (the arc's roles as slots): a run
is raised only if they hold, so a matter too small to tell raises
none (a flood that sent nobody from their home).

min_career_days.description: Days since play began before it may be raised.

opportunity.description:
An opportunity: the director times its arrival (parsed and inert:
no opportunity arc is written yet).

raise.description: Conditions over simulated state at a jurisdiction; never the ledger.

rank.description:
How it ranks for the places for arcs (`director.arcs_active`) and
for the chapter's lead: a `crisis` (a flood, a plant closing) is
never kept out of a place by a `matter` (a zoning fight, a debt), and
leads a chapter over a standing arc. Omitted: a matter.

sides.description: For stand-in players and the opening frame (task A4).

stages.description: The first stage is where a run starts.

standing.description:
A standing arc (DEC-109 §7): one the calendar raises every chapter
of its kind, so a calm town still has a turn. It runs beside the
director's cap on arcs (`director.arcs_active`), and a material arc
outranks it for the chapter's lead.

ArcRank.description:
How an arc ranks for a place (`ArcDef::rank`): later variants outrank
earlier ones.

oneOf.description: A standing matter of the town: rules, a debt, a scheme.

Something physical happening to the town: water in the streets, a
works closing.

agrees.description:
They agree: the beat is done, and its own `sets`, `relief` and
`effects` apply after this reply's.

teaches.description: What the reply teaches about the arc (task A3).

when.description: Slots `speaker` and `player`, the arc's roles, the run's marks.

id.description:
Role id: a Fluent argument (`$steward`, `$steward_role`, `$hood`)
and the slot conditions name.

optional.description: The arc runs without it (beats and effects naming it are skipped).

ArcStopStages.description: Which stages of an arc stop a skip.

oneOf.description: None.
Its turn: the stage marked `climax`.
Each one.

ArcStops.description: The moments of one kind of arc that stop a skip (`InterruptWhen::ArcStage`).

idle.description:
A stage with nothing for the player to do stops a skip too, and so
does an exit. Without (the default), a stage stops a skip once a
beat of it is the player's to take, and an exit never does.

lead_or_actor.description:
A stage counts only for a run that leads the chapter, or one the
player can act in now (a beat of the stage is theirs to take: they
hold the power its decision needs, they are in the race).

raised.description: Being raised stops a skip, whatever its first stage offers.

oneOf.description: The whole jurisdiction.
A bound neighbourhood.
A bound neighbourhood and those next to it.

The area where the hazard damaged the largest share of homes (those
not yet repaired); where a strike fell evenly, where most people
are away; else the most exposed to it.
The area least pleased with the player (where a crisis bites).

asker.description: Who asks (the role `asker`): a person cast like a dilemma role.

big.description:
A big ask: kept, a favour is owed to the player; accepting it ends
the director's relax phase.

cooldown_days.description: Days before this template is offered again.

deadline_days.description:
Days to keep it, drawn in [min, max] (the lower half in a term after
a re-election). Absent: until the vote on the bill a `vote` need names.

detail_key.description:
The situation, with the cast (and `$history`: `kept`, `broken` or
`none`, the asker's last ask) as arguments.

fresh_days.description:
Not offered when the player did what its first need asks (a deed in
the deed log) within this many days ("no town hall there in 180 days").

from.description: Where offers come from (default: the weekly draw).

keep.description:
Effects when kept, broken and declined (or left unanswered). A subset
of the narrative effects: `opinion`, `approval`, `standing`, `record`,
`favour`, `learn`, `money`.

min_career_days.description: Days since play began before it is offered (ENGAGEMENT §4.7).

name_key.description: The ask in a few words ("Say something about the closure").

public.description: Others see it: breaking it is public (approval, Standing, the press).

roles.description: Further roles (a bill, a neighbourhood, an official), cast after the asker.

triggers.description:
U1's conditions on the live state and the cast (never `knows`:
asks are aimed at the player, DEC-091).

AskFrom.description: Where an offer comes from (ENGAGEMENT §3.2 "Comes from").

oneOf.description:
The weekly draw at the sliding rate. An asker cast `goal_holder` is
someone whose NPC goal names this ask (`goals.jsonc` `ask`).

A canvass: someone on the doorstep of the canvassed neighbourhood
(`doorstep_chance` a canvass), cast among its residents.

A conversation: the person the player talked with
(`doorstep_chance` a conversation).

The player asked around about someone (a conversation about them
within `talked_about_days`): that person asks.
An arc's `ask` beat (DEC-109): offered only by a run, with its cast.

asker_kept_mult.description:
A person whose earlier ask the player kept is this much more likely
to ask again; one whose ask was broken, this much (callbacks).

doorstep_chance.description: Chance a canvass (or a conversation) brings a doorstep ask.

history.description: Resolved asks kept for views and the lab.

intent_by_open.description: Open asks → factor (points `[x, factor]`, linear between them).

intent_by_quiet.description: Days since the last offer → factor.

max_open.description: Offered and accepted asks at once (a hard cap; promises are not counted).

new_per_month.description:
The base rate of new offers a month, governing and in a campaign: the
two intent curves multiply it.

per_asker_cooldown_days.description: Days before the same person (or party) asks again.

respond_days.description: An offer lapses unanswered (as declined) after this many days.

talked_about_days.description: How far back "the player asked around about someone" reaches (days).

AttitudeDef.description:
An attitude dimension (DEC-075): an issue every cohort, politician, and
party holds a position on, in [-1, 1]. Registry order is load order (files
by path, then item order); the engine stores attitudes densely in that order.

key.description:
Short key used in policy signatures, party-name words, and Fluent keys
(`conviction-pro-<key>`, `conviction-anti-<key>`), e.g. `redistribution`.

AttitudeSeed.description:
Starting-opinion model for one attitude. A cohort's position is
`by_class + by_age + by_neighborhood + regional offset + noise`, clamped to
[-1, 1]. Each region draws its own cultural offset once per attitude.

by_class.description: Lean by income class: `[low, middle, high]`.

noise_sd.description: Standard deviation of each cohort's individual variation.

regional_sd.description: Standard deviation of each region's cultural offset.

AttributionParams.description:
Pass-through of a law's direct counts to what it added, net (the
ledger's "added" estimates; measured on twins by the audit).

homes_net.description:
Share of a public programme's completed homes that private building
would not have built anyway (1 − the starts it displaces).

jobs_net.description: Sector jobs added per job a subsidy supports (or a programme creates).

wage_floor_net.description: Low incomes' rise per unit of wage-floor uplift.

AudienceDef.description: Who follows an outlet: relative weights by income class and age band.

max.description: At most this many groups (never more than five in all).

of.description:
For crowds: [`OF_RACE`], [`OF_HERE`] (the default), or an area or
place role of the arc.

power.description: For `members`: the power their posts list.

AudienceFrom.description:
Where an audience's groups come from (§2.2). The engine binds each to
live state; none names a place or a body.

oneOf.description: The areas one level down from where the scene is.
Income classes inside one area.
The communities present in an area.
Where a cast place's workers live (until plants give it: the area).
The holders of posts with a power, one group each.
One cast person.
A crowd's approval of the player among those who know them.
A member's support: opinion, a shared party, a favour owed.
A person's opinion of the player.
A person's opinion less what they are demanding (they start against).

AudienceWeight.description: How a crowd's groups are weighed.

oneOf.description: By voters (`count × turnout`).
One each.

default.description: The option a draft gets when it names none (default: the first).

line.description: Fluent key, with the cast as arguments.

quote_fallback.description:
The speaker quotes their most salient memory of the player in this
line (arguments `memory`, `subject`, `year`); this key is used when
they remember nothing.

BeatWeight.description: A beat's weight in the chapter's budgets (task A2).

oneOf.description: Anyone but the player.
Bills of these policy templates.
A template that answers the town's live crisis (its `policies`).

A template that answers this worry (the `policies` of the crises
that sharpen it).
A promise's chosen answer (its `answer` argument).

BindDef.description:
What a slot binds, and how it is chosen (§2.3). Candidates are inside
the instance's jurisdiction, taken in id order, ranked by `pick`; ties go
to the lowest id.

oneOf.description: A place of one of these kinds.

drivers.description: Only places whose kind has one of these sector drivers.

oneOf.description: A neighbourhood.

hazard.description: Exposed to this hazard at least `min_exposure` (DEC-090 D8).

lacks.description: Place kinds it has none of.

of_slot.description: The neighbourhood of a bound place.

oneOf.description: A Named or Principal character.

in_slot.description: Lives or works in a bound neighbourhood.

oneOf.description: The town's power broker (a town's instance; unbound elsewhere until M7).
A sector.

of_slot.description:
The sector of a bound place (its kind's drivers, the
jurisdiction's largest matching sector).

oneOf.description: The live crisis (of one of these kinds).
A hazard.

in_slot.description: Its exposure in a bound neighbourhood (else the town's).

BodyDef.description:
A collective that holds seats (DEC-017): a council, an assembly, a
chamber. Its id is how procedures, content and saves refer to it (DEC-098:
no code names a body).

calendar.description:
Its own election calendar (a chamber elected off the tier's cycle);
default: the tier's.

id.description: Unique across the constitution's tiers; at most [`PostKey::MAX`] bytes.

member_key.description:
The word for one member (`councillor`): Fluent `role-<member_key>`,
and the role word content uses (topics, lines, conditions, nomination
gates). Unique across the constitution, and never an office's id.

seats.description:
Seats of an at-large body (required when its constituency is
`at_large`; a `ward` body has one seat per constituency).

works_at.description: Where members work: a place kind (`places.jsonc` `key`).

ally_above.description: An ally at or above this opinion; a rival at or below `rival_below`.

BorrowingParams.description:
Borrowing costs (`finance::accrue`): spread = the tier's spread +
`per_ratio` × (debt ÷ a year's revenue − the tier's `free_ratio`), from 0
to `max_extra`.

free_ratio.description:
Debt, in years of revenue, that lenders do not price, by tier
(local, regional, national).

max_extra.description: The most the spread rises above the tier's.

per_ratio.description: Added spread per year of revenue owed beyond `free_ratio`.

spreads.description: Spread over the policy rate at a prudent debt: local, regional, national.

BrokerParams.description:
What the power broker does (M6 note 27): leans on votes in their
interest, backs a candidate, and what knowing them opens to the player.

back_min_opinion.description: The broker backs no one they think less of than this.

back_money.description:
Campaign backing: money a week to the candidate the broker favours,
and the organisation's contacts (canvass-equivalents) a week.

back_values.description:
How much the broker thinks of a candidate: their opinion of them,
plus this × how far the candidate's views match theirs (−1..1).

cooldown_days.description:
A stand against them (opposing, exposing) is not offered again
within this many days of the last.

expose_member_opinion.description:
Exposing them through the press (the press's gaffe risk applies):
on success each member's opinion of the broker and approval among
those who resent them; either way their opinion of the player; on a
gaffe, approval among everyone (× room).

favour_opinion.description:
Doing them a favour: their opinion of the player, and approval among
those who resent them (× room; usually negative).

lobby_sway.description:
Lobbying the broker: sway on each member of the bill's body, × how
far they go along with the broker. The broker refuses below
`lobby_min_opinion` of the player.

officeholder_influence.description:
The influence of a broker with no organisation (an officeholder),
in place of an occupation's `influence`.

oppose_resent_approval.description:
Opposing them openly: approval among those who resent them and those
who depend on them; their opinion of the player; and the opinion of
the player of each member who likes them (× their liking, 0..1).

press_occupations.description: Who an exposé is told to (occupation ids: the press).

vote_pull.description:
The vote model's `broker` term: the pull on a member's lean on a
bill in the broker's interest, × the broker's influence × how far
the member goes along with them (0 when they loathe the broker, 1
when they admire them; ½ when indifferent).

BudgetCategory.description: Budget categories (mirror the finance domain's categories).

CalendarAbsent.description:
What being expected and staying away costs (`BEING_THERE.md` §5.5;
owner's answer 2: small, shown a turn ahead, at most one a turn).

opinion.description:
Opinion change (≤ 0) of the player among the stored people who were
there, in the event's part.

CalendarAttendee.description:
Who comes, by routine: one rule, for exactly one of a post's role word,
an occupation or a special role (as a routine is for). While the event
is held, in its part, a person it covers goes to the venue with this
chance (a keyed draw per person and day), before their own routines.

CalendarCadence.description: How an event recurs, counted against turns (`BEING_THERE.md` §5.1).

oneOf.description: Every turn, on the day played (it never chooses the day).

The town's community meeting night (one weekday per town, keyed by
the seed): held when the day played falls on it.

The jurisdiction's legislature sits (the routine event `session`): a
law-making stage falls in the turn, or the day played is its regular
sitting day.
Once a month, on a keyed day of the month (in `months`, if listed).
Once in each month of `months` (a term's start), early in it.
Once a year, on a keyed day in one of `months`.

crowd.description: Extra passers-by at the venue while it is held (how full it looks).

expected.description: Who is expected (any rule): only the player's absence costs.

months.description: Months (1–12) an occasion falls in (`month`: any, if empty).

names.description:
Its names (Fluent keys, with `$town`): each town keeps one, a keyed
pick, so two towns' years differ.

parts.description:
The parts of the day it can be held in, the first preferred. A
second event on the day takes a part no earlier event holds; an
occasion with none left is reported as having happened.

requires.description: Situation conditions (slot-free) that must all hold in the town.

scope.description: The tier it belongs to (instances are keyed by its jurisdiction).

talk.description:
People here have time to talk: presence counts double for
familiarity (`BEING_THERE.md` §6.2).

venue.description:
A place kind (`places.jsonc` `key`), or `legislature` (where the
jurisdiction's legislature sits). A town without one has no such
event.

verbs.description: Visit verbs done there while it is held (`actions.jsonc`).

weekday.description: The weekday an occasion's date moves on to (the show on a Saturday).

CalendarExpected.description: Who is expected to be there (no office named, DEC-098).

oneOf.description: Whoever holds this power in the event's jurisdiction.

Holders of a post with this role word (a body's `member_key`, an
office's id) in the event's jurisdiction.
The holder of a districted seat whose district holds the venue.

ad_persuasion_share.description: Persuasion of one ad buy, as a share of one canvass contact's.

ad_saturation.description: Each further ad in a turn is worth this fraction of the last.

contact_memory.description: Share of recent contacts remembered each week (diminishing returns recover).

diminishing.description: Each repeated contact in a neighbourhood is worth this fraction of the last.

npc_contacts_per_week.description: NPC campaign effort in abstracted races (contacts per week per candidate).

npc_effort_base.description: Abstracted NPC effort scales with `npc_effort_base` + oratory.

approval.description: Approval gained per unit of room (× fit × fresh × season × same turn).

awareness.description:
Share of the remaining awareness gap closed (× `max(fresh,
awareness_floor)`).

awareness_floor.description:
Awareness is built at least at this share of the full rate, however
stale the doorsteps (canvassing stays the way to be known).

campaign_mult.description: Approval multiplier while the player is a candidate in an open race.

contact.description:
Campaign contact scale (a full day on the doorsteps; × the same-turn
cut).

hood_decay.description:
Freshness per remembered visit to a neighbourhood (DEC-097 §1,
ENGAGEMENT §2.1): `fresh = hood_decay ^ visits`.

hood_decay_campaign.description: The same in campaign season, when doorsteps are expected.

keep.description: Share of a neighbourhood's remembered visits kept each month (30 days).

same_turn_mult.description: Approval and contact multiplier for a second canvass in one turn.

CanvassMatch.description:
Canvassing on an issue (DEC-091 "ignorance costs effectiveness"): the
approval gain is multiplied by `1 + match_bonus × (salience − 1)`, at
least `floor` and at most `ceiling` (salience: the neighbourhood's felt
level of that worry over the mean of its worries).

ceiling.description:
The most a well-chosen worry multiplies the gain by (a neighbourhood
with one overwhelming worry would otherwise make a canvass several
times as strong). Older packs: no cap beyond 2.

CareerLadderDef.description:
The career ladder (DEC-098; audit §7.5). Acts are not tiers: the summit
is one office, an act of its own. Validation checks that the player has
a path to the summit (DEC-017).

acts.description: The acts of a career, in order.

summit.description: The office (or body) at the top of a career.

CareerParams.description:
Careers (DEC-011, DEC-076): the record of visible work, the party's
patience, Mandate and viability, name recognition, and election results.

invisible_record.description:
Name recognition kept each month, and while the record is below
`invisible_record`.

loss_viability.description:
After a loss: viability changes by `loss_viability` +
`loss_viability_per_margin` × margin (margin ≥ −0.5), and Standing.

mandate_rate.description:
Mandate: monthly pull toward 50 + `mandate_per_net_approval` × net
approval among the ward's voters.

nomination.description:
What a party asks before it nominates the player for a post, keyed
by role word (an office's id or a body's `member_key`; DEC-098).
A post with no entry has no gate.

npc_diligence_rate.description:
NPC officeholders' monthly record gain per unit of diligence, and the
weights of integrity and ambition in diligence.

officeholder_funds.description: Officeholders' yearly war-chest income: base + per unit of oratory.

record_fade.description: Share of every record lost each month.

record_gain.description: Record gained per piece of visible work (the player and NPCs).

scandal_keep_yearly.description: Share of scandal damage kept each year.

thin_record.description:
Party patience: monthly Standing change below a thin record and above
a strong one.

viability_rate.description:
Viability: monthly pull toward a mix of Mandate and Standing (this
share Standing).

win_mandate_base.description:
After a win: Mandate = `win_mandate_base` + `win_mandate_per_margin` ×
margin (at least `win_mandate_min`), and track gains.

CaseworkParams.description: Casework (ENGAGEMENT §3.4): "Sort it out" at the town hall, one slot.

success_out_of_office.description: Out of office the player can only chase it up.

Cast.description: How a role is cast from live actors in the player's town.

oneOf.description: The town's power broker (DEC-077 §1).
The player's named rival.

The holder of an office in the player's town (when it is not the
player): `office` names it by constitution id; by default the town's
executive (the office that signs its ordinances; DEC-098). The old
spelling `{ "type": "mayor" }` reads as the executive.

A Named person with one of these occupations: one with a stake in the
live crisis first, then leaders, then the most influential.
A council colleague (not the player).
Someone the player owes a favour (the largest debt).
A bill before the council.

sponsored_by.description: Sponsored by the person cast in this role.

oneOf.description: The sponsor of the bill cast in `role`.

A neighbourhood of the player's ward: the one least pleased with
the town government (where a crisis bites).

A law of one of these templates (any, if empty) in force or being
built in town (`building`: only one still being built), sponsored by
`sponsor`.
The person whose goal raised this request (requests only).

The colleague closest to the player (the highest opinion of them):
someone to lean on, or to blame.

discovery_days.description: A hidden fact becomes discoverable within this window after it happened, [from, to] days.

hazard_hold_days.description: A hold on hazards in the player's town lasts this long before it is reviewed.

hazard_max_defer_days.description: A held hazard strikes at most this many days after it was drawn.

recession_hold_months.description: The onset of a global recession may be held at most this many months.

CharacterGenParams.description: Generation of characters (DEC-031): personality and competency ranges.

drift_sd.description: Lazy yearly updates of Named characters: value drift (SD per year).

family_chance.description: Chance a Named character is family of a local politician.

first_impression_sd.description: A Named character's first impression of the player: normal, this SD.

personality.description: Personality axes are drawn uniformly in this range, plus offsets.

trust_initial.description: Trust in someone they have no history with (0..1).

values_sd.description: Named characters' values: their home cohort's view plus noise of this SD.

CharacterParams.description: Characters, memory, relationships, and town character (DEC-031, DEC-077).

ChoiceReplyDef.description: One possible reply to a talk choice.

agrees.description: The person agrees: the need is met.

ClockDef.description:
A stage's deadline: a keyed draw in a range of days from its entry or
before the jurisdiction's budget year turns, or (not yet) the subject's
own date.

before_budget_year.description:
Days before the jurisdiction's budget year turns, [least, most]: a
keyed draw between them (never before tomorrow). The budget
calendar is the simulation's; where in the range is the draw's.
With `days` too, the draw is where the two ranges overlap (else at
the first day `days` allows).

placed.description:
A director-owned clock (DEC-033 B; STAGED_ARCS §3.2): the draw
stays inside `days`, and a storyteller with a tension curve places
it inside the chapter's climax window where the two overlap, so the
turn falls where the chapter wants it. Never a date the simulation
owns.

oneOf.description: The date the simulation owns (a review, a forecast). Not yet: A5.

Commodity.description:
A world commodity an industry sells or buys (the economy's three price
indices, in their order).

CommunityDef.description:
A community (DEC-075): a cohort dimension beside age band and income
class. Every neighbourhood holds age × class cohorts for each community.
Registry order is load order (files by path, then item order). The base
pack ships one community, so the dimension costs nothing until an
expansion adds another (an Indigenous nation, an immigrant community, a
linguistic minority).

attitude_offsets.description:
Added to the seeded attitudes of this community's cohorts, by attitude
key (omitted = 0).

immigration_share.description:
Fraction of international immigrants who join this community (the
remainder community takes whatever the others leave).

share.description:
How much of each neighbourhood's population belongs to this community.
Exactly one community omits it: that community takes the remainder
(in the base pack, `community.general` is everyone).

turnout_offset.description: Added to the seeded turnout propensity of this community's cohorts.

CommunityShare.description:
Share model for a community: in a neighbourhood the community's share of
every age × class group is `base + by_neighborhood[kind] + regional
offset`, clamped to [0, 1]. Each region draws its offset once (sd
`regional_sd`). Where the communities with a share model add up to more
than 1, they are scaled down to 1; the remainder community takes the rest.

base.description: Share everywhere, before the neighbourhood and regional terms.

by_neighborhood.description: Added by neighbourhood kind (omitted kinds are 0).

regional_sd.description: Standard deviation of each region's offset (0 = none).

ConcernDef.description:
A voter concern (DEC-078 decision 3): something that worries a town,
read from an indicator, and the issues (attitudes) it makes voters weigh.
Registry order is load order.

attitudes.description:
The attitudes behind the concern, by key. The magnitude is how much a
worried town weighs that issue; the sign is the side worried voters
lean toward (used to rank concerns by neighbourhood).

level.description: How the indicator's value becomes the concern's level.

name_key.description: Fluent key of the concern's name, e.g. `concern-jobs`.

talk_key.description:
Fluent key of the concern as people name it in talk: a lower-case
noun phrase for mid-sentence use ("the rent"), as sectors have; the
name is used without one.

oneOf.description: The speaker's home neighbourhood (what worries them; conversations).
The town.

The neighbourhood where it is said or done (a line heard, a
conversation's place, a place visited).

Condition.description:
A condition on live state: the jurisdiction's situation, the player, a
person in a slot (a cast role, or a conversation's `speaker`, `about`,
`player`), a conversation, or where something is said or done.

oneOf.description:
A live crisis in the town (`crises.jsonc`; of this kind, if given) at
least `min_severity` severe: `$crisis_key` (the most severe such
crisis). `live_crisis` is the old spelling without a kind.
An engine indicator of the town within [min, max].

One worry condition, felt or measured, of the town or a
neighbourhood: one of the listed concerns (`concern`, or any of
`concerns`) is among the `top` strongest worries `of` the town
(default), the speaker's home neighbourhood, or the neighbourhood
here, `by` how residents feel them (`felt`, as the notebook ranks
them) or by their measured levels (`measured`; the town's are its
priorities, its three strongest, kept with its character). Defaults
follow the spelling: with one `concern`, measured, top 3 (the dilemma
spelling); with `concerns`, felt, top 1 (the conversation spelling).
Gives `$concern_key` (the name) and `$concern_talk_key` (the noun
phrase of talk) of the strongest listed worry that holds.

The town has a defining industry (with one of these drivers, if
given): `$industry_key` (the sector as residents name it).

A plant closed in the town within this many months (the event log):
`$industry_key` (the closed plant's sector), `$jobs`.

A disaster struck the town within this many months; with `hazard`,
one of that kind whose damage is not yet repaired (the environment's
footprint: a strike that damaged no home does not count).

A law of one of these templates is in force or being built in the
town (`absent`: none is).
The town has this water (`any`: also a waterfront neighbourhood here).
No water at all: no river, no coast, no waterfront here.
The town has a power broker: `$broker`.
The player has a named rival in the town: `$rival`.
The rival's record of visible work within [min, max] (0..1): `$rival`.

A scandal running in the town (DEC-034) about this subject:
`$subject` (their name), `$fact_key`.

A story about the town within the last eight weeks (an overheard line
retells it: `$outlet_key`, `$headline_key` and the headline's own
arguments, added by the protocol).

The player's name recognition among the residents here within
[min, max] (0..1): `$player`.

Approval of the player among the residents here (−1..1) within
[min, max]; only where at least a fifth know them: `$player`.

The industry of the place here (its kind's `sector`) is shedding jobs
in its town, at least `min` of the way to full shedding
(`visit.outlook`: 0 just below `shedding`, 1 at `shed_full`):
`$industry_key`.

Someone of one of these occupations is here now (people's routines;
not the player).
It is one of these parts of the player's day.

The jurisdiction is in this phase: a campaign for one of its posts is
running (`campaign`), or none is (`governing`).
The player's next election is within this many days.
At least this many months since play began.
The player is (or is not) standing in a running campaign.

The player holds one of these posts (DEC-098): role words (a body's
`member_key` or an office's id, from the run's constitution), `any`
(any post) or `none` (out of office). `role` is the one-word
spelling (`{ "type": "office", "role": "councillor" }`).

The player holds a post for this jurisdiction whose constitution
lists this power (read through the constitution, never an office's
name: `requires_power`).
A track within [min, max].
The player's campaign funds within [min, max] (currency units).

The player answered `template` (with `option`, if given; a default
that happened counts) between `min_days` and `max_days` ago
(ENGAGEMENT §4.4: consequences of the player's own choices). Roles in
`same_cast` are cast as they were in that decision.

The player sponsored a law of this status, between `min_age_days`
and `max_age_days` old (since enacted; a pending bill since it was
introduced): the law cast in `slot`, or any. `chance` is the share of
such laws that count, a keyed draw per law and condition, so the same
law always gives the same answer (ENGAGEMENT §4.4, §4.7).

The player knows the subject at least this well (DEC-091; default
`heard`), its roles from the cast. A subject naming several places
holds if any is known. Framing only (refused where a condition
decides whether something happens: the world does not wait for the
player).

The player's ledger (DEC-091) holds the subject, named from the
conversation, within [min, max]: the subject's arguments. Framing
only.

The person in the slot has one of these roles: occupation ids, or
role words of the constitution's posts (a body's `member_key`, an
office's id; DEC-098). With `is: false` it holds when they have none
of these roles (so a general line can leave a role to its own lines).
The person in the slot has one of these traits.
A personality axis of the person in the slot within [min, max] (0..1).
The person in the slot holds this goal (DEC-032).
Their opinion of the player within [min, max] (−100..100).
Their trust in the player within [min, max] (0..1).

They remember the player doing one of these (memory kinds; the most
salient): `$memory_key`, `$subject_key`, `$subject_kind`, `$year`.

The player owes them a favour (or, `owed_to_player`, the reverse): `$n`.
With `is: false`, none is owed (the debt was paid, or never was).

The person in the slot sponsors a bill the player can still vote on,
and a yes would cost the player: their ward leans against it, their
party's line is against it, or a promise they hold forbids it (the
first such bill, the first bind that holds). `$law_key` (the bill's
template), `$bind` (`seat`, `party` or `promise`).

They have (or have not) met the player before now: talked with them
(a line of theirs in the conversation guard), or met them on an
earlier day (a `met` memory). Meeting a passer-by today is not
having met them before.

How well they know the player's face (DEC-114 §5): at least
`at_least` (`face`, `nod`, `ours`), or, with `is: false`, less.
Familiarity is a deed (presence, `BEING_THERE.md` §6.2), so it may
choose a line; content names a word, never a number.

They are (or are not) the town's power broker (local-only). When
they are: `$broker`, `$broker_place`, `$stake_key`.

They are (or are not) the player's rival in the town (local-only).
When they are: `$rival`.

The player's party line on the bill cast in `slot` runs against the
mood of the player's ward.
The player can still declare a vote on the bill cast in `slot`.

The speaker would tell the player at least `min` about the subject
(what they know, capped by discretion): the subject's arguments.

The speaker's voice (`talk_voices`) is one of these, so a line (an
opener) follows the voice the closers use. Not allowed in a voice's
own conditions.

What the conversation is about (the `about` subject): one of these
kinds (empty: any subject); for a place, one of `places` (place kinds;
empty: any) and, if `workplace` is given, the speaker's own
workplace (`true`) or not (`false`): where they work, or where their
post sits; for a neighbourhood, if `home` is given, the speaker's home
(`true`) or not, if `office` is given, inside the jurisdiction or
district of a post the speaker holds (`true`) or not, if `works` is
given, where the speaker works (`true`) or not, if `here` is given,
where the conversation happens (`true`) or not, and if `tied` is
given, any of those four (`true`) or none of them (`false`: somewhere
the speaker has no reason to know). With `is: false` it holds when
the subject is not that (or there is none).

This concern is among the `top` worries (measured) of the
neighbourhood bound to `slot`.

The neighbourhood bound to `slot` is exposed to this hazard at least
`min` (0..1; DEC-090 D8).

The sector bound to `slot` has lost at least `min` of its jobs in the
jurisdiction since the baseline (E1; a share, 0..1).
The place bound to `slot` is open (DEC-090 D3).
The place bound to `slot` has closed.

A run of this arc is at one of these stages (any, if empty) in the
jurisdiction: for overheard lines, topics and whatever holds while a
stage does. With `here`, only where that role of the run is: its
place, or a place or street in its area.
The run has (or has not) this mark. Inside an arc only.

The run finished a scene (DEC-112) whose outcome is one of
`outcomes` (`won`, `split`, `lost`, `absent`; any, if empty) and
whose result (Σ weight × change in lean, per mille) is within
[`min_pm`, `max_pm`]: the scene the player played, read where the
ending is decided. `beat` (`<stage>.<beat>`) names one scene of
the arc; omitted, the latest. Inside an arc only.
The run's heat within [min, max] (0..1). Inside an arc only.

Days since the run's current stage was entered, within [min, max].
Inside an arc only.

The share of the residents of the area cast in `slot` who are
staying elsewhere after a disaster, within [min, max] (0..1; without
bounds it always holds): `$away` (people). Inside an arc only.

The share of the homes damaged in the area cast in `slot` when the
arc was raised that are repaired, within [min, max] (0..1; without
bounds it always holds): `$homes` (damaged then), `$repaired`.
Inside an arc only.

The last run of this arc in the jurisdiction that reached a turn
reached it at this stage (`is: false`: at another, or none has).
Climax memory by variant: the same turn does not come two years
running. Inside an arc only.

Days until the jurisdiction's budget year turns (its treasury closes
its books), within [min, max]: the budget calendar.

The balance of the jurisdiction's treasury over its last closed
budget year, as a share of that year's revenue, within [min, max]
(negative: it spent more than it took; no closed year reads 0;
without bounds it always holds): `$books` (`short`, `over` or
`level`: beyond a hundredth either way) and `$gap` (the share in
whole per cent, never negative).

One party holds (or, `is: false`, none holds) more than half of the
posts for the jurisdiction whose constitution lists this power; with
`share`, at least that share of them (0.6: a majority with a seat
to spare in a body of seven).

The share of the holders of posts for the jurisdiction that list
this power (the player not counted) who would back the player,
within [min, max] (0..1; without bounds it always holds): those of
the player's party, those whose opinion of the player is at least
`opinion` (default 10), and those who owe the player a favour.
`$backers` and `$members` (counts).

The last race the player stood in is decided, and they won it (or,
`won: false`, lost it). Never holds while they have stood in none.

The person in the slot sponsors a bill the player can still declare
a vote on.

A named plant in one of these states (none given: any): with `slot`,
the plant at the place cast in that role of an arc (the open one,
else the last that closed there); without, any plant in the
jurisdiction's towns. With `closes_within_days`, under notice with
its date at most that many days off. `$plant_key`, `$stem`,
`$works_key`, `$product_key`, `$jobs`; under notice also
`$closes_day`, `$closes_month_key`, `$closes_year` (the date).

An open proposal of this policy family is on the table in the
jurisdiction: `$proposal_<slot>` for each of its place and
neighbourhood slots (their names), `$proposal_<slot>_key` for its
sector, crisis and hazard slots. People are never named.
Any one of these holds (the first that does gives the arguments).
The old spelling of a `crisis` without a `kind`.

ConnectorDef.description:
What carries a road, a path or the railway over water, a creek or the
track (§6.1, §7.7). The generator picks, per crossing, the first entry in
load order that allows it.

art.description: Art keys by role; `kit` is required.

town_class.description: Town classes it is built in (empty: everywhere).

ConnectorKind.description: The kind of crossing, as the town map's connectors name it.

oneOf.description: One seat per generated ward / district.
The whole jurisdiction.

career.description: The career ladder: the summit and the acts (DEC-098; DEC-004).

param.description: The parameter the per-unit costs multiply.

per_capita.description: Fixed annual cost per resident (price level 1).

per_capita_per_unit.description: Annual cost per resident per parameter unit.

per_unit.description: Annual cost per parameter unit (e.g. per dwelling).

CouncilParams.description:
How council members lean on bills, how mayors sign, and lobbying odds
(DEC-026, DEC-071 §7). Shared by the player and NPCs.

enactment_awareness.description: Public awareness a bill gains at enactment, and the share it loses each month.

mayor_own.description: The mayor's lean on a bill: own values and the town's support.

noise_sd.description: Standard deviation of each member's idiosyncrasy per bill.

own_values.description:
A member's lean: own values (weighted by 1 − pragmatism), the ward's
support (by pragmatism), and the mayor's lean.

player_opinion.description: Goodwill toward the player as sponsor, per 100 points of opinion.

sign_bias.description: Mayors sign unless their lean is below −`sign_bias`.

sunset.description:
Riders: a sunset, a pilot, each other ward's earmark, and an earmark
for the member's own ward.

vote_sharpness.description: Logistic slope from a lean to the chance of a yes vote.

sponsor_yes.description:
The sponsor's opinion of the player: a yes, a no, and a no while they
are owed a favour.

standing_loyal.description: Standing for voting with the party line, against it, and abstaining.

ward_reaction.description: Ward approval per unit of alignment × (0.5 + bill awareness) × room.

CountDef.description: The result is a count of heads, not a mean (§2.4).

CountNeeds.description: How many members must end with the player.

oneOf.description: More than half.
At least two thirds.

CoverageParams.description: Story selection, scandal heat, and perception (DEC-034).

heat_end.description: A scandal ends below this heat.

heat_keep.description: Heat kept each week (a scandal fades).

hostility_interest.description: Extra interest per unit of disagreement between an outlet's lean and the subject.

min_score.description: Stories below this score are not run.

newsworthiness.description: Newsworthiness by severity (a scandal at full heat).

regional_access.description: Interest of a regional (nation) outlet in a town affair, × severity weight.

stories_kept.description: Stories kept (for the newspaper and the audit).

town_news.description: Neutral town news (closures, disasters, laws) the local paper runs.

typical_budget.description: Budget at which an outlet runs its `stories_per_week`.

CrisisDef.description:
A kind of live local crisis (DEC-077 §1), read from an indicator with
hysteresis: it begins at `begin`, ends below `end`, and its severity runs
from 0 at `end` to 1 at `severe`. Registry order is load order and breaks
ties between equally severe crises.

concern.description: The concern it sharpens (a concern id), if any.

policies.description:
Policy templates that answer it: NPC agendas favour them while the
crisis lasts.

CueDef.description:
The street cues of a fault (S7; drawn by the client in B4): while it is
open, while it is being repaired, and once repaired (for `new_days`).

Curve.description: Response curve mapping an input (0..1) to a score (0..1).

oneOf.description: m·x + b, clamped to 0..1.
`lo` below `x`, `hi` at or above.

CycleLengths.description:
Phase lengths of the pacing cycle for one kind of chapter (ENGAGEMENT
§4.3), in days: `[from, to]` ranges are keyed draws.

build_up.description: Minor beats only, then a peak.

peak_max.description: A peak lasts until its decision is answered, at most this long.

relax.description: Minor beats only, then the next build-up.

relax_after_climax.description: The relax after a session's climax (default: `relax`).

CycleParams.description:
The pacing cycle (ENGAGEMENT §4.3, after Left 4 Dead's AI Director and
RimWorld): build-up, peak, peak fade and relax, across chapters.

setback_relax_mult.description: The relax after a setback is this much longer.

DayPart.description:
A part of the day played (DEC-013, DEC-114): the three standard slots and
the late-night one. The engine reads it from the player's progress
through the turn (`characters::routines::day_part`).

bold_personal.description: Weight added to the personal sources: × boldness.

grudge_personal.description:
Weight added to the personal sources by a grudge (a trait in
`grudge_traits`, or a memory of the player against them).

pick_top.description: A weaker opponent picks among their best this many.

sharp.description:
Skill at or over which they read how residents feel, not what a
statistic shows, and always pick their best.

warm_question.description: Weight added to the room's question: × warmth.

weak_evidence.description:
A hidden fact held on evidence under this is kept out by integrity
at or over `integrity_bar`, and used only by boldness at or over
`bold_bar`.

DeliveredWeights.description:
Credit for a law's delivered results, in approval units per unit of
what it delivers now (its ledger's net "added" quantities and what it pays).

homes.description:
Per unit of homes added in a year (a share of the stock), felt by
the low and middle classes.

income.description:
Per unit of income paid or raised (a share of the class's income),
felt by that class.

jobs.description:
Per unit of jobs added (a share of the town's labour force), felt by
working-age residents.

DilemmaCategory.description: The weight of a decision in the director's budgets.

oneOf.description: Only ever a chapter's climax.
A significant decision (may also be chosen as a chapter's climax).
A request raised by an NPC's goal: a lightweight dilemma (minor).

DilemmaDef.description:
A dilemma (DEC-077 §4): a moment where every option costs someone, built
from live state, warned in advance, and explained afterwards.

arc_only.description:
Only presented as an arc's beat, never on its own (the old spelling
`storyline_only` still reads).

cooldown_days.description: Days before the same dilemma may be spotlighted again.

min_career_days.description:
Days since play began before the director may spotlight it
(ENGAGEMENT §4.7: new pressures year by year).

opportunity.description:
An opportunity: its arrival is timed by the director rather than
forced by a crisis (DEC-033 B).

raised_by.description:
Raised by a story or an investigation about the player, not by the
spotlight (DEC-006 fairness: never budgeted).

situation_key.description: The situation, with the cast as arguments.

themes.description:
Chapter themes it belongs to (ENGAGEMENT §4.2): a themed template is
drawn before the rest in a chapter of its theme.

DirectiveDef.description: A standing directive for a time skip (DEC-012).

concern_options.description:
`focus` only: also offer one option per concern in the registry (its
id is the concern's id, its name the concern's `name_key`).

default.description: The option a new run starts with.

DirectiveLever.description: What a directive steers in the proxy (an engine contract).

oneOf.description:
Which worry the ground game and new bills aim at (`concern`; none:
the strongest the player knows of).
How the player votes on bills (`vote`).
Effort on doorsteps and public meetings (`weight`).
Effort on raising money (`weight`).
Effort on statements to the press (`weight`).
Effort on drafting and steering bills (`weight`).

How cautious to be: the largest shown risk of a hidden act accepted
(`max_risk`) and the health below which the proxy rests (`rest_below`).

concern.description: `focus`: a concern id; none is the strongest worry the player knows.

max_risk.description:
`caution`: the largest shown chance (0..1) that a hidden act comes
out which the proxy still accepts; 0 avoids every shady option.

rest_below.description: `caution`: the proxy rests when health is below this (0..100).

weight.description: Effort levers: the relative share of the turn's slots (0 = none).

DirectorBudgets.description: Decisions and developments allowed per chapter (DEC-033 pacing model).

climax.description: Climaxes per chapter (a campaign chapter's climax is its election).

minor.description: Minor developments (requests, news of the town), [target minimum, maximum].

significant.description: Significant decisions per chapter, [target minimum, maximum].

DirectorParams.description: The narrative director (DEC-033): one file across all packs.

arcs_active.description:
Arcs running at once in a focus jurisdiction (DEC-109: one lead and
one background), standing arcs aside.

cooldown_floor_days.description: Every dilemma's cooldown is at least this many days …

cooldown_growth.description: … and the n-th use sets `max(floor, cooldown) × growth^(n−1)`.

crisis_cap.description:
Crises the player's town may carry before the director holds
exogenous hazards back (the cap on simultaneous unresolved crises).

deadline_days.description: Days to decide when a dilemma gives none.

default_profile.description: Storyteller profile of new games (a `storytellers` id).

development_spacing_days.description: Least days between two minor developments.

history.description: Resolved decisions kept for the story so far.

min_relevance.description: Least relevance for a situation to be spotlighted.

no_repeat_in_chapter.description: A template spotlighted in a chapter is not a candidate again in it.

pick_band.description:
The pick draws among candidates whose relevance is within this of the
tier's best, weighted by relevance × novelty.

post_climax_significant.description:
After a session's climax and its relax, at most this many significant
decisions (the coda): a consequence, an opportunity, or a `budget`
template.

quiet_days.description:
Nothing for the player this long (governing, campaigning): a minor
beat is spotlighted at once, in any phase (the quiet rescue).

repeat_penalty.description: Score multiplier for a template or a person already spotlighted this chapter.

session_min_days.description:
A session chapter (a budget year in office) lasts at least this many
days; a shorter one runs on to the following year.

spacing_days.description: Least days between two spotlighted decisions.

themes.description:
Chapter themes and their draw weights (ENGAGEMENT §4.2): `crisis`,
`budget`, `scheme`, `local_life` (campaign chapters take `campaign`).

tier_a_window_days.description:
A consequence (`answered`) whose window closes within this many days
is drawn first (tier A, with the arcs' decisions that are due).

Discoverer.description: Who may uncover a hidden fact.

oneOf.description: A reporter at an outlet in the subject's town (Named journalists and editors).
A political opponent: the subject's rival.
The town's auditors (money trails).
Police and prosecutors' investigators.

DiscoveryParams.description:
Discovery of hidden facts (DEC-034): whether a fact will come out is
settled when it happens (evidence × interest × access), never by the
director; when, within its evidence window, is the director's (DEC-033 B).

bands.description: Risk bands: low below [0], real below [1], high from [1].

horizon_days.description: The risk line's horizon (DEC-073: "within a year").

journalist_floor.description: Journalist access without any journalist in town (the regional press).

journalists_full.description: A town's journalists add access up to this many (a town without a paper has little).

window_strong.description: Evidence window (days after the act) at evidence 1 and evidence 0.

DiscretionBand.description: Up to (but not including) an opinion of the player, the most a speaker tells.

below.description: The band's upper opinion bound (−100..100), exclusive.

DiscretionDef.description:
Discretion: the most a speaker tells, by their opinion of the player and
their trust (the bands of the protocol's `opinion_band`).

top.description:
What the friendliest tell, with trust at least `trust_for_detailed`
(with less trust, one level lower).

oneOf.description: Those still staying away from the area: they leave for good.

DistrictAppears.description:
When a district type may be chosen. Among the eligible types the
generator picks by weighted rendezvous hashing.

hood_kinds.description: Neighbourhood kinds it can stand for.

requires_place.description: Place kinds the town must have (e.g. a mine for pit rows).

DistrictArt.description:
A district's art keys (§7.1): keys, never files. `family` is the required
last-resort parent of the fallback chain (§7.3).

DistrictBuildings.description: Filler buildings: `[kind, weight]` pairs, storeys and density.

reserve.description: Share of plots held back for growth (0..0.5).

DistrictPlots.description: Building footprints and the open ground of the district's blocks.

joined.description: Share of plots joined to the next (0..1).

DistrictSite.description: Siting preferences for the district's seed.

anchor.description: What the district is laid out around (`square`, `harbour`).

DistrictStreets.description: The district's street pattern and its parameters (tiles).

block.description: Block width range (6..40; §8: the minimum block is 6 × 5).

DrawDef.description: How often a family turns up in a run.

weight.description: Priority when several are ready at once, in (0, 10].

attribution.description:
Coefficients that turn a law's direct counts into what it added to
the town, net (its ledger's "added" entries, audit fix 5; the same
for every template).

base_dwelling_price.description: Average dwelling price at price level 1.0.

birth_rate.description: Births per adult aged 18–44 per year.

borrowing.description:
What a jurisdiction pays to borrow: a spread over the policy rate by
tier that grows with its debt against its revenue (`finance::accrue`).

commodity_volatility.description: Monthly volatility of commodity prices (log scale).

hazards.description:
How a hazard's damage and displacement fall across a town's
neighbourhoods (DEC-090 D8).

housing.description:
The town housing market: household formation, rents, prices and
private building (`economy::housing`).

industries.description:
Industries and named plants (DEC-110): the closure process, plant
sizes and siting numbers every industry shares.

migration_rate.description: Monthly share of mobile adults who reconsider where they live.

recession_depth.description: Peak fall in global demand during a recession, [min, max].

recession_monthly_chance.description: Monthly probability that a global recession begins.

tech_growth.description:
Annual structural trends of a world without a scenario bias:
technology growth, and the drift of manufacturing competitiveness.

treasury_shares.description:
How each tier's treasury splits its discretionary budget across the
budget categories at the start (DEC-098: content, not code).

unemployment_replacement.description: Unemployment benefit and pension as a share of the mean wage.

EdgeDef.description:
An edge fires when every part given holds: its conditions, the days
since the stage was entered, and the clock.

after_days.description: At least this many days in the stage.

clock_within_days.description: The clock is at most this many days away (0: it has run out).

EffectDef.description:
One real engine effect of choosing an option (DEC-073: costs and benefits
are simulated, not narrated).

oneOf.description:
The role's opinion of the player changes (scaled by their personality,
as every opinion change is), remembered as `memory` if given.

Approval of the player among voters (−1..1 scale), by income class
(0 low, 1 middle, 2 high; empty = all), in the ward or the town, or in
the neighbourhood cast in `neighborhood`.
Name recognition among voters.
Campaign funds (currency units; negative is a cost).
Time this turn (an option that needs more time than is left cannot be chosen).
Visible work in office (0..1 scale).
A favour: the player owes the role one (or, `owed_to_player`, the reverse).
The player repays a favour owed to the role (a kept promise).

The player declares a vote on the bill in `role` (the council-vote
rules apply: party, ward, and sponsor react).

The bill in `role` gains a rider: a ward project for the player's
ward, or a sunset (its sponsor agrees, or it is the player's bill).
The council-vote rules price it (other wards' members grate at a
ward project; a sunset makes passage easier and the law temporary).

ward_of.description:
A ward project for the ward of the councillor cast in this role
(the vote it buys); the player's ward without one.

oneOf.description:
The role repays a favour they owe the player by backing the player's
side of the bill in `bill` (their lean moves as a traded favour does).

The player drafts a bill of this template (parameters not given take
their defaults).

A borderline or illegal act (DEC-034): a hidden fact that may come to
light (its risk is shown before the player commits, DEC-073).

with_role.description: A cast person in on it (named in the fact).

oneOf.description: The player's answer to a story about them (scandal decisions only).

The player's answer to an investigation (investigation decisions
only); `blame` names the cast ally in `role`.

The player learns something (DEC-091): a subject raised to a level,
never lowered.

A hidden place is revealed (DEC-090 D7): places of these kinds in the
neighbourhood cast in `role` (or the home neighbourhood of the person
cast in it), else in the player's town, become `known`.

An inspection of the town's polluting industry (audit fix 8): its
operators must clean up, so the region's pollution falls at once by
`pollution` × the town's share of the region's polluting jobs (then
drifts back as industry keeps working), and the town's largest
polluting sector loses `output` of its demand for `months` months.
Effect requests to the environment and the economy, caused by the
player's answer.

cycle_offset.description: Elections fall in years where `year % term_years == cycle_offset`.

partisan_ballot.description: Party labels appear on the ballot (otherwise a nonpartisan race).

ElectionTiming.description: Whether a tier votes on the same day as a higher tier (DEC-071: turnout).

EndingDef.description:
One way an act ends (DEC-006; the endings registry, DEC-098 note). The
first entry whose condition holds ends the act.

acts.description: Act ids (the constitution's `career.acts`) it can end; empty: any.

facts.description: What the epilogue reports, in order.

text_key.description: Fluent key of the epilogue's text (arguments: the facts by key).

title_key.description: Fluent key of the ending's title.

EndingFact.description: A fact an epilogue reports, computed by the engine.

oneOf.description: Posts held this act.
Years the act lasted.
Laws in a works category (`legacy.works_categories`).
Notable decisions taken.

EndingTone.description: How an ending reads on the epilogue screen (presentation only).

EndingWhen.description:
When an act ends (DEC-006; DEC-098 note). Posts are read through the
constitution: its acts, its powers, its terms.

oneOf.description: The player holds a post of a later act of the career ladder.

The player holds a post of this act with all these powers, which
they did not hold when the act began (e.g. the tier's executive).
The player stood in an election this act, lost, and holds no post.
Something happened to the player this act.
The run's status is one of these.
A track at or under `value` (disgrace, the political wilderness).

The act has lasted `terms` full terms of the post the player holds
(its `term_years` in the constitution), and they hold it.

The player stepped away from politics (M6 note 23: the run is
abandoned, after one confirmation, at any time).
Any of these.

ExchangeParams.description: Every constant of the exchange (§5.6). Placeholders, all of them.

act_votes.description: Added to `act` when the body would back it.

answer.description: The size of the other side's answer, by the kind it answers.

backfire.description: What a line that does not stand costs.

cold.description: Round 1's bite when the player did not know what was coming.

cover.description: How far a kind covers a prompt it answers.

heard_floor.description: A worry learned only second-hand lands at this share.

member_line.description: A member is with the player at or over this lean.

prompt_variants.description: Wordings written for each prompt and each line of the player's.

public_share.description: A public fault counts at this: people have heard it.

spill.description: What a targeted line gives the groups it did not name.

tiers.description: Overrides by tier (DEC-098): dotted paths, as a scene's `params`.

visits_full.description: Visits to a place that make `heard` land in full.

visits_keep.description: How long a visit counts (the ground game's `keep` a year).

voted_share.description: A law the player only voted for counts at this.

walk_away.description: A table is lost under this lean.

worries.description: How a law's ledger speaks to each worry.

worry_match.description:
A bill is about the worry whose attitudes it lines up with at least
this much (else it is no worry: `fit.flat`).

effects.description: Effect requests to the owning systems, each gated on the run.

follow_up.description: An arc that may follow (task A2).

headline_key.description: A story the outlets may run as it ends.

legacy_key.description:
The Legacy record's line for how the arc ended (its `ArcEnded`
entry; the career card, M6 note 23). Without one, the exit's own
text (`key`) stands for it.

delivered.description:
What laws deliver (audit fix 3), felt by those they reach; zero
without laws.

rent_growth.description: Per point of real rent growth (a year).

service_budget.description:
Per unit of the town's budget against the level its budget rule aims
for (1 at need): baseline services that programmes crowd out and
taxes fund (audit fix 3).

services.description: Per unit of service improvement from laws in effect.

unemployment.description: Per point of local unemployment rise beyond the national rise (a year).

unemployment_gap.description:
Per point of local unemployment above the nation's, now (the
benchmarked level: a closure costs until the place recovers).

ExpiryDef.description: When an open instance with no bill goes away (§2.4).

cooldown_months.description: Months before it can open again in the same jurisdiction.

grace_months.description: … or when its trigger has not held for this many months.

max_months.description: … or this many months after it opened.

ExposureDef.description:
The exponents of an industry's demand formula (DEC-110): each named
factor raised to its exponent, multiplied together.

import_exposure.description:
Import exposure: how hard foreign competition bites (the exponent
on the nation's manufacturing competitiveness; a later tariff on its
goods works through this term).

labour_cost.description: Elasticity to the town's unit labour costs.

low_pay.description: Share of its jobs a wage floor prices (0 = none of them).

markets.description:
Its own weights across markets (market id to weight); omitted
markets take the market's own `share`.

prices.description:
Price exponents by good (a good id with a price index): above zero
for what it sells, below for what it buys.

stock.description: The region's stock it draws on, if any.

water.description: Exponent on the region's water availability.

FairnessParams.description:
Fairness (DEC-006): a warning before any terminal ending. A track at or
past its threshold is warned about (pinned event, the pocket's alerts).

legal_jeopardy.description: Warn at or above these (100 is the terminal end).

repeat_days.description: Repeat a warning while the track stays in danger after this many days.

response_days.description: An ending may follow a warning only after this many days (a chance to respond).

standing.description: Warn at or below these (0 is the terminal end of each track).

Familiarity.description:
How well someone knows the player's face, in words (DEC-114 §5): the
bands of the relationship's familiarity (`characters.jsonc`
`familiarity`). Never shown as a number.

oneOf.description: A stranger.
Knows the player's face: greets them by name.
A nod: says what is on their mind without being asked.
One of ours: a regular who counts the player as one of their own.

FamiliarityParams.description:
Familiarity (DEC-114 §5, `BEING_THERE.md` §6.2): a deed, built by
presence and kept as one small number on a person's relationship toward
the player. Shown in words by these bands, never counted.

decay.description: Lost each month without a meeting (no sighting in `idle_days`).

ours.description:
"One of ours" from this, with an opinion of the player above
`ours_opinion`.

presence.description:
Added on a turn the player is where they are (once a turn a person);
`event` at a calendar event with time to talk.

FamilyBaseDef.description: What every version of a family has, as in a policy template.

works.description: A works project every version builds (DEC-099).

FamilyKnowledgeDef.description: How the player finds out about a proposal (§2.7, DEC-091).

public.description: In the paper when it opens (heard by all).

area.description: Where it applies (at most one axis per family sets it).

excludes.description: Options it cannot be combined with (`"axis.option"`).

fixed.description: Hidden parameter values its mechanisms use.

months.description: Added to the implementation time (at least 1 month overall).

needs.description: A tier or competence it needs (M7): shown unavailable in M6.

signature.description: Added to the base signature per attitude (clamped to −1..1).

works.description: A works project this option builds (DEC-099).

adopt_opinion.description:
The sponsor's opinion of the player when the player adopts their
version (−100..100 scale).

amend_opinion.description: Opinion per axis changed away from the sponsor's preset.

free_steps.description: Slider changes within this many steps of the preset are free.

max_open_per_jurisdiction.description: Proposals open at once in one jurisdiction.

rarity.description: The chance a family of each rarity is in a run's deck.

FamilyPatch.description:
A targeted change to another pack's family, applied in pack order
(DEC-092: "mods can … patch them"; §5 question 10).

oneOf.description: Change how often it turns up.
Add an option to an axis.
Remove an option from an axis.
Add a sponsor.
Remove a sponsor.
Never draw or open it again (bills and laws continue).

asset.description: What it is on (`street_light`, `drain`): the asset, for cues.

feeds.description: The worry it adds to while open (a concern id).

pays.description: The budget line of the town's treasury that repairs it.

restore.description: Condition (0–1) the neighbourhood gains when it is repaired.

text.description:
Its Fluent prefix: `<text>name` ("the street light"), `<text>what`
("the light on { $hood }'s streets is out").

sway_share.description: The share of a favour trade's sway an offered favour gives.

FitParams.description: How much a group cares about a subject, by the worry's rank there.

flat.description: A subject that is no worry (a thin record, a promise to turn up).

FrameDef.description:
An arc as an opening (DEC-101 §2): the seat the player arrives in and
the draft's line. The run is raised the day play begins, so its first
stage's beats are on offer on turn 1 (the first-beat guarantee); the
ally and the opponent are the arc's `sides`; the clock is its stages'.
(The design's hidden fact to uncover, `secret`, is not built.)

pitch_key.description:
The draft's line (`pitch-*`), with the arc's text arguments as
they stand on the day play would begin (its cast, `place`, `town`,
the dates and its `facts`).

post.description: Which seat of the entry post the player takes.

FramePost.description: The seat a frame puts the player in.

donor_ties.description: Approval lost among low-income voters, per unit of awareness.

raised.description: Money raised: uniform in [min, max] × (0.5 + oratory). NPCs too.

standing.description: Standing gained (the party likes a fundraiser).

GatedEffect.description:
An effect, applied when every `when` holds and no `unless` does (the
run's marks, heat and days; simulated state).

oneOf.description: The role's opinion of the player, remembered as `memory` if given.

Approval of the player in an area role (−1..1), by income class
(empty: all).
A favour: the player owes the role one (or the reverse).
The player's record of visible work (0..1).
The player's Standing.

Damaged homes in an area role are repaired `repair` times as fast
for `months` months (the environment applies).
People of an area role leave their town (the population applies).

A change voted into the next budget of the arc's jurisdiction: one
`category`'s line of its discretionary budget, or every line,
× `factor` when its budget year turns (finance applies, to the
tier's own treasury; DEC-098). A line funded or cut.
The run's own heat.

The player learns of a cast person, or of the worries of a cast
area, to a level (the player applies; never lowered).

Relief on the margin of the plant at the place cast in `place` for
some months (DEC-110: the economy applies it, and its own rule
still decides the review).

One favour the player owes the role is paid off in another coin
(the characters domain applies; nothing if none is owed).
Approval of the jurisdiction's government in an area. Not yet: A5b.
A place's state for the dress pass (boarded, marked). Not yet: A5a.

unless.description: Applied unless all of these hold.

GatewayKind.description:
Where trade physically passes (DEC-110, the seam for foreign trade): a
kind of place. A port today; a border crossing and a rail head are kinds
a later layout can place. An industry's siting can weight one, an
industry can name the one its external trade ships through, and a later
disruption can hit one.

GeoCondition.description:
Geography conditions (each a field of the town's geography, §6.5). Every
condition given must hold; per-mille ranges are 0..1000.

shore.description: Shore kinds (`beach`, `rocky`, `cliff`); the town's must be one of them.

GoalDef.description: An NPC goal template (DEC-032): emerges from circumstances plus personality.

ask.description:
When the goal needs something done later: an ask (`asks.jsonc`) whose
asker is cast `goal_holder` (ENGAGEMENT §3.1).

conditions.description: Conditions on the town and the holder (role `holder`).

max_days.description: A goal is given up after this many days (or when its conditions fail).

personality.description: Personality axes of the holder within [min, max].

request.description: When the goal needs the player: a request (a dilemma of category `request`).

traits.description: The holder has one of these traits (empty = no requirement).

GoalDrive.description: How a goal drives the NPC AI (DEC-030 utility AI; the same rules as the player).

oneOf.description: No AI change: the goal only surfaces as a request.

Leans against the player's bills (added to their council lean) and
lobbies against them.
Leans toward the player's bills.

Ranks bills that answer the town's live crisis higher (added to the
agenda bonus, like `npc.crisis_agenda`).

GoalGrant.description: A goal a role holds while a stage lasts (task A2).

occupations.description: Named people with one of these occupations.

officeholders.description: Council members and the mayor (not the player).

GoodDef.description:
A good (DEC-110, the seam for foreign trade): what a product is, for a
tariff or a trade deal to name. Every product belongs to one. A good
may carry one of the world's price indices: the prices industries sell
and buy at are read through this registry.

price.description:
The world price index this good's price is (none: no price index;
an industry cannot be exposed to its price).

GrantDef.description:
One grant: every subject of a kind that a selector picks, raised to a
level. Selectors: `home` (the player's home neighbourhood), `ward` (the
neighbourhoods of the player's ward), `town` (the zone's town), `here`
(the place being introduced: introductions only), or a place kind.

GrantSubject.description: The kind of subject a grant gives.

oneOf.description: The town's worries (`which`: `town`).
Neighbourhoods' worries (`which`: `home`, `ward`, `town`, `here`).

Who really runs things (`which`: `town`; `here`: only if the broker
is found at the place).

Everyone holding a post in the town, as people (`which`: `town`):
the members of its bodies and the holders of its offices, as the
constitution defines them (DEC-098). The word is a grant subject,
not a body id.

The people found at places (`which`: `town` for every place, `here`,
or a place kind such as `union_hall`).
The rival's plans (`which`: `town`).
Who supports each standard policy (`which`: `town`).
The proposals on the table (`which`: `town`).

How the place's industry is doing in its town (`which`: `here`;
visits only).
Pollution and hazards at the place (`which`: `here`; visits only).

The real need the place's service meets (`which`: `here`; visits
only).

Gravity.description:
How serious a hidden fact is (DEC-006 Legal Jeopardy): a lapse of
ethics, misconduct in office, or a crime.

HazardParams.description:
Where a hazard falls within a town (DEC-090 D8). The town-level rolls and
damage are unchanged; these set how they are shared by neighbourhood
exposure, who is displaced, and how fast a neighbourhood recovers.

leave_share.description:
Share of a neighbourhood's damage whose mobile adults leave the town
for good (floods, storms and earthquakes; wildfires displace only for
a while).

max_hood_damage.description: Most of a neighbourhood's homes one strike can destroy (a share).

max_relative.description:
Most a neighbourhood's hit can exceed the town's average (× the
town's damage), for damage and for how hard residents feel it.

repair_rate.description: Monthly share of a neighbourhood's damaged homes repaired.

return_rate.description: Monthly share of the displaced who return home.

temporary_share.description:
Adults displaced for a while per unit of a neighbourhood's damage:
they stay in less-hit neighbourhoods (or the next town) and return.

anyOf.description: `@slot`: a family's hazard slot (composition replaces it).

HazardRef.description:
A hazard a mechanism names: a hazard, or (in a policy family) `@slot`,
the hazard bound to that slot. `"flood"` parses as before.

HeardSubject.description: Whose scandal a condition is about.
