HeatDef.description: Heat: one number per run, 0 to 1, in the arc's own domain.

floor.description: Heat never falls below this simulated reading.

HeatFloor.description: A floor on heat: an indicator of the jurisdiction × `scale`.

HiddenSpec.description:
A borderline or illegal act: what it is, how serious, how much evidence
it leaves, and who might uncover it (DEC-034, DEC-073: the risk is shown
before the player commits).

discoverers.description: Who could uncover it (empty = every discoverer).

evidence.description: How much evidence it leaves (0..1): a paper trail is high, a quiet word low.

HoldParams.description: The chance a claim stands up, by how well it is known.

oneOf.description: Where the conversation happens.
The speaker's home neighbourhood.
The subject (a neighbourhood, or a place's neighbourhood).

HookDef.description: A moment that teaches the player about a proposal.

oneOf.description: Arriving at a place of one of these kinds in the town.
Arriving at the bound place, or the streets of the bound neighbourhood.
Meeting, lobbying or trading a favour with the bound person.
Doing this action in or with the bound thing.
Arriving where this service is offered.
Talking to the bound person on this topic.
The sponsor asks for a meeting this many months after it opens.

HotspotDef.description:
A hotspot: a rectangle of tiles, the actions and services offered there,
and the tile the player stands on to use them.

actions.description: Action keys from this place kind's `actions` (or `late_night`, for a late hotspot).

HouseholdParams.description:
Doors and households (DEC-114 §2, `BEING_THERE.md` §3): door slots per
neighbourhood, households generated on demand at a door, the doorstep
exchange's chances, and the bounded doorstep records.

adults.description:
Adults in a household, [min, max]; children by the neighbourhood's
children per adult.

agree.description:
Listening at this many doors of a street that name the same worry
teaches the neighbourhood's worries (`known`).

ask_base.description:
Asking for their vote (in a campaign) or a poster: the chance is
`ask_base + ask_view × view`, within [`ask_min`, `ask_max`].

not_in.description: Chance nobody answers at an occupied door (keyed by door and day).

owner_by_class.description: Chance a household owns its home, by class (low, middle, high).

records_per_hood.description:
Doorstep records kept a neighbourhood (the oldest forgotten), and the
days after which a household forgets a call.

residents_per_door.description: One door slot per this many residents (adults and children) ...

street_doors.description: Doors a canvass knocks at most (a street).

view_sd.description:
The spread of a household's view of the player around its cohort's
(−1..1, a keyed normal draw).

warm.description: A view at or above this is warm; at or below `cool`, cool.

HousingParams.description:
The town housing market (`economy::housing`). Rent clears vacancy;
households form more slowly as rent takes more of an income, so rent is
bounded by incomes; builders answer price over cost and vacancy. The
starting state is an equilibrium: at the target vacancy and the neutral
rate, private starts equal their baseline.

adults_per_household.description: Adults per household at the reference rent burden.

adults_per_household_range.description: Adults per household, [fewest, most]: the bounds of doubling up.

base_growth.description:
Baseline building beyond replacing demolitions, as a share of the
stock per year.

build_cost_share.description:
Build cost as a share of the starting price (below 1: building is
mildly profitable at the starting equilibrium).

capped_vacancy_signal.description:
Share of the vacancy signal builders still answer while a rent cap
binds (a shortage promises no rise in rents they may charge).

demolition_rate.description: Share of the stock demolished per year.

headship_elasticity.description:
Elasticity of adults per household to the rent burden: households
double up (or form later) as rent takes more of an income.

price_adjustment.description: Monthly share of the gap to the target price closed.

reference_burden.description:
A year's rent over a middle-class income at which households form at
`adults_per_household`.

rent_response.description: Monthly rent growth per unit of vacancy below target.

rent_yield.description:
Gross rent yield at the neutral rate: a year's rent over a dwelling's
price as play begins.

risk_premium.description:
Premium over the real rate in the user cost of housing (sets how
prices answer interest rates).

starts_max.description: Most private starts, as a multiple of the baseline.

starts_price_response.description: Private starts per unit of price over build cost (against the start).

starts_vacancy_response.description: Private starts per unit of vacancy below target.

ImpactBasis.description:
What a coefficient multiplies: a direct quantity of the bill, as a share
of the town (so one row serves any town size). One per mechanism kind
whose effect on the town the lab measures, `spend` for what all
spending does, and `law` for what any law does.

oneOf.description:
1 for every bill: what passing any law does, whatever is in it. It
takes a place on the statute book (a bill that would have passed
does not), and no two futures are alike: its range is how far a
town with one more law strays from the same town without, before
the law's own content counts. Outcomes as shares of the town.
What the bill takes from the budget a year, over the budget.

Homes a programme adds by the ledger's own count (`homes_added`),
over the housing stock.

Homes private building adds under looser zoning (`homes_added`),
over the stock.
The share by which a cap holds rents below the market (`rent_held_pct`).

Jobs a wage subsidy or a programme adds in its sectors by the
ledger's count (`jobs_added_*`), over all jobs (over the sector's,
for the outcome `sector_jobs`). Fed by `sector_subsidy` and
`sector_capacity` alike.

The share by which a wage floor raises low incomes by the ledger's
count (`low_income_added_pct`).
A year's payment to an adult of the class, over that class's income.
The service index gained (`service_gain_pct`), as a share.
A year's revenue of the tax change, over the budget (negative for a cut).

ImpactFit.description:
How the table was fitted (what `lab impact calibrate` ran), so a reader
knows how much it rests on.

enacted_at.description: Months at which laws were enacted.

levels.description: Parameter levels each template was enacted at: `default`, `max`.

towns.description: `home`, or `classes` (the home town and one town of each other class).

twins.description: Twins run (template × level × town × month × world).

worlds.description: Worlds: `none` (a random country) and scenario ids.

ImpactOutcome.description:
An outcome the simulation computes each month and the lab samples. Every
one is a change against the same town without the law, as a share
(approval: of the 0..1 scale, so 0.01 is a point).

oneOf.description: Homes in the jurisdiction, net of private building displaced.
Jobs in the jurisdiction, net.
Jobs in a sector a mechanism names.
Typical rent.
Income per adult on low incomes.
The treasury's debt, over its yearly budget.
The service level (budget against need plus laws' gains).
Approval of the government.

ImpactRow.description:
One fitted coefficient: across the lab's twins, the 10th, 50th and 90th
percentile of (the outcome's change, less what the bill's other bases
explain) ÷ this basis, `months` after enactment.

n.description: Twins the row was fitted on.

arithmetic.description:
Mechanism and side-effect kinds the estimate states by arithmetic
alone, with no coefficient: money (`borrow`, `revenue`), protection
against a reference event (`hazard_protection`), and the side
effects, whose size scales with their mechanism's in every template
and so cannot be told apart from it on twins (their consequences are
inside the mechanism's rows). Every other kind in use needs a row.

tiers.description:
Tiers the rows were calibrated for. A bill of another tier gets no
estimate, not a guess (DEC-098).

Indicator.description:
Engine-provided measures of a municipality, recomputed monthly. Concerns
read them; situational policies (DEC-077) will use them as unlock
conditions. Adding one is a code extension point (one variant, one
computation in `mandate_sim::concerns::indicator`, and a test).

oneOf.description: Unemployment rate (0..1).
Change in the unemployment rate over the last year (points, 0..1 scale).
Annual rent of an average home as a share of a typical (middle-class) income.
The region's pollution index (0 clean, about 0.2 at start, up to 3).
Annual property tax on an average home as a share of a typical income.
The town's debt as a share of its annual budget.

Services delivered against need, as a shortfall: 1 − (the town's
discretionary budget in real terms per head, against the level its
budget rule aims for) − the service gains of laws in effect. 0 at
the start; above 0 after cuts, below 0 with better services.
1 just after a disaster, fading to 0 over two years.

Share of the town's jobs lost over the last year (0 when jobs grew):
a plant closure or a failing industry.

IndustryDef.description:
An industry (DEC-110): a registry level under a sector. The sector stays
the group that totals, worries and map layers read; a sector with
industries is a split sector, whose state is the sum of its industries.
Registry order is load order (files by path, then item order).

base_wage.description: Mean annual wage per worker at price level 1.0.

cyclicality.description: Elasticity of demand to the global cycle.

export_share.description:
How much of its demand is external (sold to the markets) against
domestic (`home`): demand is `export_share × external + (1 −
export_share) × home`.

home.description:
What its domestic demand reads, as weights (omitted: national
consumption).

link_power.description: Exponent on the supply term the links make.

products.description: What its works make: at least one.

ships_through.description:
The gateway its external trade ships through, if one: what a later
disruption at a gateway reaches.

talk_key.description: Fluent key of the industry as residents name it (a noun phrase).

weight.description: Share of the sector's jobs in a generic economy.

world.description: How its index moves in each market (one walk per market).

IndustryLink.description:
A local supply link (DEC-110): this industry runs on what another
industry, or a whole sector, does nearby. No goods move; the link reads
the upstream's jobs against their ten-year average.

from.description: An industry id or a sector id.

local.description: Share read from the town itself; the rest from the rest of its region.

IndustryParams.description: The closure process and plant sizes shared by every industry (DEC-110).

boom_line.description:
A boom reopens a works when the industry's demand has averaged over
`boom_line` and the stock is over `boom_stock`, `boom_months` after
it closed at the earliest, at `boom_size` of the closed plant's size.

factor_months.description: Months in the average of each demand factor that names the cause.

full_line.description:
It is back on full time when demand is at or over this for
`short_months` months (above the short line, so hours do not flap).

link_range.description: Supply links read upstream jobs over their average within this range.

max_industries.description:
Siting: the most industries a town keeps in one split sector, by
settlement class (rural, town, city, metro).

max_town_share.description: The most of a town's jobs one plant holds when it is placed.

min_capacity.description: An industry smaller than this in a town sheds no firms (jobs).

min_plant.description:
The smallest named plant by settlement class: rural, town, city,
metro (jobs).

min_share.description: Siting: a share of the sector under this folds into the others.

name_forms.description:
How plant names are formed, as weights: the town, a family, a word
from `works_words`, the district.

new_plant_margin.description:
A plant that opens during a run draws its margin this much higher
(newer works are the last to go).

notice_gap_months.description: Months between new notices in one town (waived in a recession).

notice_line.description:
A notice is served when it is under this for `notice_after_months`
months running.

notice_months.description: A notice's length in months, [least, most]: the one draw.

pool_share.description:
While a closed works waits to reopen, the share of what idle labour
draws each month that gathers toward it; the rest grows the unnamed
firms at once, so a town's recovery does not wait for the works.

reprieve_line.description:
A notice is lifted when demand is at or over this for
`reprieve_months` months before the date.

short_line.description:
A plant goes on short time when its margin-adjusted demand is under
this for `short_months` months running.

small_decay.description:
Monthly shrinkage of an industry's unnamed firms while its demand is
under the notice line.

town_sd.description: Siting: standard deviation (in logs) of a town's own draw.

trend_months.description: Months in the long average of jobs that anchors the supply links.

works_words.description: Words a works is named by ("the Albion mill"). Fictional (REQ-001).

world_range.description: Bounds of an industry's world index.

InteriorLight.description:
The room's light: the lamps' colour, how much of the night's grade reaches
inside (0..1), and unseen ceiling lights.

cast.description:
How someone is here (the place view's `here_as`: presiding, member,
works, visitor) → the spot roles they take, in order of preference.

door.description: The entrance's column in the front wall.

extras.description: Staff roles drawn as scenery where nobody present takes them.

place.description: The place kind (`places.jsonc` key) it furnishes.

version.description: A change that moves anything for the same seed bumps it (DEC-085).

wall_h.description: The back wall face's height, px.

key.description: Fluent key of the reason shown ("The skip stopped: …").

InterruptWhen.description:
What stops a time skip (DEC-012 interrupts). Interrupts fire on a
change during the skip: what was already so when it began does not.

oneOf.description:
A track crosses `threshold`: rises to it or above, or with `below`
falls to it or under.

A decision opens with one of these weights, or (`about`) one that
answers a story or an investigation of the player.
A story about the player breaks, at least this grave.
An election the player stands in is called (they are a candidate).
A bill the player sponsors reaches a vote within `days`.

Someone's request of the player (or a promise to them) falls due
within `days`. With `offers`, an ask still on offer counts too: it
waits for the player's answer and stops the skip as its last day to
answer nears (DEC-102 clause 7). Without, an offer left unanswered
through a skip lapses as declined. `big_offers` counts only the big
asks on offer: a small one may lapse, a big one is the player's to
answer.

A staged arc in the player's focus reaches a moment that is the
player's to meet (DEC-102 clause 7). Which moments, by the kind of
arc: `material` for an arc that is not standing (a flood, a plant),
`standing` for one the calendar brings round (the budget year, a
campaign's rival). A hidden stage never stops a skip. The message is
given `arc` (the template's id), `stage` and `run`.
The run's status changes (prison, release, the end of the career).

awareness.description: Public awareness of a bill when it is introduced (player and NPCs).

oneOf.description: The tier above.

JusticeParams.description: The legal path (DEC-006 Legal Jeopardy): investigation, charges, trial, sentence.

charge.description: Chance of charges at the end, × (evidence + `charge_evidence_base`).

convict_base.description: Conviction: logistic(base + evidence × evidence − lawyer + mood × (0.5 − approval)).

disqualify.description: Chance a crime conviction disqualifies from office.

fine.description:
Sentences: a fine (currency, by severity), removal from office
(chance for misconduct; always for prison), prison years for crimes.

fine_standing.description: Standing and viability lost to a fine or a removal.

long_years.description: A sentence this long (years) or a disqualification ends a career.

official_bonus.description: Extra when auditors or investigators found it.

open.description: Prosecutors' interest: chance an investigation opens, × evidence.

open_days.description: Days from discovery to the decision to investigate, [min, max].

release_standing.description: Out of prison: Standing and viability set to at most these.

track_decay.description: Legal Jeopardy falls this much a month with no open case.

track_investigation.description: Legal Jeopardy floors by stage (the track shows the case).

trial_days.description: Days from charges to trial, [min, max] (at least the fairness response time).

KnowledgeEffects.description: The effectiveness terms, applied symmetrically by the shared formulas.

lobby_logit.description:
A logit term on lobbying odds by the actor's knowledge of the
target as a person (NPCs, who keep no ledger, use `known`).

KnowledgeParams.description: The knowledge parameter block (`kind: "knowledge"`, one file across packs).

fresh_days.description: A reading older than this many days is shown as stale.

leads_cap.description: Leads kept at once (oldest dropped first).

local_option.description:
"Start with local knowledge" (off by default), applied on top of the
profile. Never `detailed`, never hidden places.

primer.description: A party contact's primer on entering a new zone.

starts.description:
Start profiles. The draft of three (DEC-036) names one per
background; until then every run uses `default_start`.

visit_all.description:
Given at the first visit to any place in a zone (beside its kind's
introduction).

oneOf.description: The town's worries.
The worries of the speaker's own neighbourhood.

The worries of any neighbourhood (`who` says whose: an officeholder's
jurisdiction, where someone works).
The councillors and the mayor, as people.
Support for policies (bills before the council and the menu).
Proposals the speaker sponsors (DEC-092).
Proposals of the speaker's workplace (DEC-092).
The people who work where the speaker works.
The speaker, as a person.

KnowsDef.description:
One rule of speaker knowledge: who knows what, to what level. NPCs keep
no ledgers: what a speaker knows is derived from these, never stored.

KnowsWho.description: Who knows a rule's subject (kept in code; the levels are content).

oneOf.description: Anyone from the subject's town.
An organisation leader (an occupation with `leader: true`).
Someone whose stake covers the town's defining industry or its live crisis.
The town's power broker.
A politician.
A sponsor of proposals (DEC-092; nobody until policy families exist).
Someone with a workplace.

Someone holding a post whose jurisdiction (or district) covers the
subject: a neighbourhood inside it, its town, the town itself
(DEC-098; read from the constitution's posts, never by office name).

Someone whose workplace (their own place, or where their post sits)
is in the subject's neighbourhood.

LawStatus.description: Which of the player's laws a `sponsored_law` condition reads.

oneOf.description: Enacted and in force (or being built).
Before the council.
Repealed, expired, defeated or withdrawn.

Layout.description: How the scene is laid out on screen (presentation only).

oneOf.description: A strip of groups (a debate, a public meeting).
A row of faces with a count (a hearing).
Two short lists: what is asked and what is offered (a negotiation).

LeadDef.description: A lead posted when the proposal opens: who or where would know more.

else.description: Used when `to` names an unbound slot.

oneOf.description: The first place of this kind in the town.
A person in a slot (`speaker`, `about`).
The streets of a neighbourhood.

Whoever the speaker knows who would know the lead's subject, judged
from public facts (their post, their work, where they live): the
person expected to know it best. No such person: no lead.
The bound person or place.
A place of this kind in the town.
The streets of a bound neighbourhood.

LedgerReading.description:
A worry's reading in a law's ledger, and the amount that answers it in
full (§3.1, `record`).

full.description:
The amount that is a full answer; with `per_thousand`, for every
thousand residents of the law's jurisdiction.

key.description: A ledger key, or a prefix ending in `_` (`jobs_added_`).

LegacyParams.description: The Legacy record's settings (DEC-006, DEC-100: a record only).

max_entries.description: Entries kept (the oldest notable decisions go first).

notable.description: Decisions of these weights the player answered are notable.

rating_plays.description:
The career card (M6 note 23): plays of a race per rating, each on a
fork under its own luck, by the engaged stand-in (DEC-102 clause 6).
A race is rated when it opens with the player in it, and the
opening as play began.

works_categories.description: Laws whose budget category counts them among the player's works.

LegalResponseKind.description: How the player answers an investigation (DEC-006 Legal Jeopardy).

oneOf.description: Wait and see.

LegalResponseParams.description: Responses to an investigation (the player's decision, NPCs by personality).

blame_charge.description: Blaming an ally: the charge chance × this; the ally's scandal valence + this.

cooperate_charge.description: Cooperating: the charge chance × this, evidence + this, sentence × this.

lawyer_charge.description: A lawyer: the charge chance − this, the conviction logit − this.

stonewall_strong.description:
Stonewalling: at evidence ≥ `stonewall_strong` the charge chance + this
(obstruction), below it − `stonewall_relief`.

Level.description:
How much the player knows of a subject. Ordered; a subject's level only
ever rises (identities never fade, DEC-091).

oneOf.description: Nothing.
A rumour or a name.
Met or seen first-hand.
From the right place or person.

LobbyArguments.description:
The arguments of a lobbying conversation (M6 note 29). Each replaces
the plain pitch's ties term (the member's opinion of the player /
`council.lobby.opinion_scale`) in the lobbying logit with its own.

broker.description:
The broker (who wants what the player wants): × the member's
compliance with the broker (0..1).

exchanges.description: Lobbying exchanges with one member on one bill a week.

party.description: Their party's line (on the player's side): × the member's loyalty.

rally_sway.description:
An ally or the party whip brings others: sway per member ×
(their opinion of the one asked / 100, plus their loyalty if in the
same party), clamped to 0..1.

ward.description:
Their ward: × the ward's support for the bill (−1..1, on the
player's side).

word.description: The player's word (an ask of theirs kept): × (2 × trust − 1).

LobbyEffects.description: The player's lobbying (the odds and the sway gained are in `council.lobby`).

arguments.description:
Lobbying as a conversation (M6 note 29): the arguments the player
can make, beside the plain pitch.

late_night_legal.description: Legal jeopardy of a late-night deal.

opinion_success.description: The target's opinion of the player after a success and a failure.

trade_gain.description: Sway bought by trading a favour.

LobbyParams.description: Lobbying odds and sway (player and NPCs alike).

gain.description: Sway gained on success: uniform in [min, max] × (0.5 + negotiation).

integrity.description: Personality (DEC-031): − this × (target's integrity − 0.5) in the logit.

opinion_scale.description: Ties with the player: the target's opinion of them divided by this.

same_party.description: Ties between NPCs: the same party, or not.

skill_scale.description:
Logit of success: `skill_scale` × (skill − 0.5) + `pragmatism` × the
target's pragmatism + `bias` + ties (+ `late_night`).

LocalConcernParams.description:
Neighbourhood concern levels: the town's indicators are measured per
town; each neighbourhood feels them through its own residents, homes and
surroundings. A neighbourhood's indicator is the town's × a relative
factor, scaled so the residents' weighted mean over the town is 1 (the
town's own figure is unchanged). Tax burden and budget stress are felt at
the town's level everywhere; a recent disaster by its impact (DEC-090 D8).

job_loss_decline.description:
Weight of a sector's decline since play began (1 − jobs ÷ its
starting jobs) beside its cyclicality in who feels the town's job
losses.

jobs_sector_tilt.description:
Share of the jobs a district's sectors lost since play began, beyond
the town's average, that adds to its unemployment rate (0: by income
class alone).

pollution.description:
Exposure to the region's pollution by neighbourhood kind, before
workplaces and water.

pollution_floodplain.description:
Added exposure × the district's flood exposure (0..1): the low land
by the river or shore takes the runoff.

pollution_next_door.description: Added exposure per polluting workplace in a neighbouring district.

pollution_workplace.description:
Added exposure per polluting workplace (an industrial or extraction
workplace in `workplaces`) in the district.

rent.description:
Rent by neighbourhood kind, relative (every kind > 0). A district's
rent burden is its rent over its residents' incomes (the mean of
rent ÷ income across its income classes).

rent_growth.description:
Elasticity of a district's rent to how much faster it has grown since
play began than its town (residents against their baseline).

sector_kinds.description: A district's extra share of a sector's workers by its kind.

workplace_affinity.description:
A district's extra share of a sector's workers per workplace of that
sector in it (half for one next door).

workplaces.description: Place kinds (snake-case keys) that employ a sector driver's workers.

MapLayerBreaks.description: How a sequential layer's class breaks are drawn.

oneOf.description: About as many towns in each class (for skewed figures).
Classes of equal width from the lowest town to the highest.

detail_key.description:
Categorical layers: Fluent key of the readout's detail, given `$pct`
(the category's share or index, 0–100).

id.description: Content id, `map_layer.<name>`. The layer picker lists layers in load order.

label_key.description: Fluent key of the layer's name in the picker and the legend.

note_key.description: Fluent key of a short note under the legend (how the figure is chosen).

source.description: The town figure the layer shows.

unit_key.description: Fluent key of the legend's units line (what the numbers are).

MapLayerFormat.description: How the client writes a layer's numbers.

oneOf.description: A whole number (residents).
A number per km².
A share (0..1) written as a percentage.
An amount of money.
A category's name (categorical layers).

MapLayerMidpoint.description: A diverging layer's midpoint (its grey class).

oneOf.description: The national figure: the towns' figures weighted by population.
A fixed value in the figure's units.

MapLayerScale.description: How a layer's classes are coloured.

oneOf.description: One hue, light to dark: magnitude.
Two hues either side of a grey midpoint: above or below a baseline.
A fixed order of a few hues, the rest folded into "Other": identity.

MapLayerSource.description:
A figure the engine serves per town for the map. The names are the field
names of the map's town figures (`MapTownFigures`), so an unknown source
fails when the content loads.

oneOf.description: Residents.
Residents per km² of the town's land.
Share of the labour force out of work (0..1).
Middle-class gross income per working-age adult, a year.
Typical monthly rent.

The industry that defines the town: the largest relative to its
national share, public employment aside (DEC-077 §1). Categorical.

The town's strongest natural resource (farmland, timber, minerals,
fishing, energy, scenery). Categorical.

MapLegendDef.description: A layer's legend: how many classes, and how they are drawn.

breaks.description:
Sequential layers only (default quantile). A diverging layer's classes
are equal steps either side of its midpoint.

classes.description:
Sequential: 3–7 classes. Diverging: an odd 3–7 (the middle one grey).
Categorical: 1–3 named categories (the most common), the rest folded
into "Other". Three is the most a map can tell apart for every reader
(the colours are validated for all pairs).

MarketDef.description:
A market (DEC-110, the seam for foreign trade; DEC-087): a place an
industry sells to outside the country. The base pack has one, the rest
of the world. An industry's external demand is the sum over markets of
its share in the market × the market's index for the industry × the
market's access. A neighbouring nation added later is another market,
with an index its own economy drives. Registry order is load order.

access.description:
Access as the world begins: 1 is open trade. A tariff, a treaty, a
dispute or a closed border changes it later.

share.description:
Its weight in every industry's external sales (shares are these
weights over their sum); an industry may set its own
(`exposure.markets`).

MechanismDef.description:
Typed mechanism primitives (DEC-024). Policies never write outcomes
directly; the domain models compute consequences from these.

oneOf.description: Raise a service level; `per_unit` = index gain per parameter unit.
Annual cash transfer per adult in a class, in currency at price level 1.
Extra dwellings built per year.
Multiplies private housing starts by (1 + per_unit × param).

Caps how fast rent may rise while the law is in force: at a level
above 0, rent may grow at most `loosest` + `per_unit` × (level − 1)
a year (nominal). Level 0 caps nothing. The housing market does the
rest: excess demand shows as a shortage, returns and starts fall,
and rent catches up once the cap lifts.
Subsidy as a share of a sector's wage bill; jobs respond with `elasticity`.

sector.description: Content key of the sector, e.g. `sector.retail`.

oneOf.description: Wage floor as a share above the low-class market wage.
Reduces damage from a hazard by `per_unit` × param (capped at 0.9).
Changes the local property tax by `param` percentage points of value.

Finance (DEC-092 families): this share of the annual cost is added to
the jurisdiction's debt instead of being spent from its budget.

Finance: income that offsets the cost, `per_capita` per resident (of
the area) plus `per_unit` × param a year, at price level 1.
Economy: structural jobs in a sector, `per_unit` × param.

MediaParams.description: The media parameter block (one file across all packs).

late_night_deal.description: Late-night deals and fundraising (M5c's hidden facts).

npc_acts.description: NPC acts by id (a `shady_actions` key, or `donor_deal`), with their payoff in funds.

MemberFit.description:
How a member or a person cares (§5.3): a base, and weights on who they
are. The result is kept in `[min, max]`.

demand.description: What a `demand` takes from a person's starting lean.

goal.description: A subject that matches one of their goals counts as this.

loyalty.description: × loyalty, for one of the player's party, by kind.

memory.description:
Added when they remember something good of the player; taken when
something bad.

party_step.description: A member's starting lean: opinion ÷ 100, plus these.

forget_below.description:
A memory whose salience falls below this has faded into the
relationship baseline and is forgotten.

principal.description: Memories kept per Principal and per Named character.

decay.description: Fading per year (salience × e^(−decay × years)); near 0 persists.

magnitude.description: How much it mattered (0..1): its salience when fresh.

opinion.description:
Opinion change (−100..100) when the engine does not set one itself
(the player's actions take theirs from `actions.jsonc`).

sentiment.description: How the holder felt about it (−1..1).

MindKind.description: What the person may bring up when asked the open question.

oneOf.description: Something they have asked of the player and are waiting on (asks).
Their main worry: what is felt most where they live.
Gossip they hold about someone they know.

MoveKind.description: The kinds of line (§3.1), in the order the list shows them.

words.description: Optional whole-word list mixed in with generated names.

NeedDef.description:
What keeps an ask: an ordinary command the engine checks (DEC-032: no
fetch quests), or casework. An ask's needs are met in order.

oneOf.description:
A declared vote on the bill cast in `role` (a bill before the
council); due by its vote unless `deadline_days` says otherwise.

No yes vote on (and no sponsoring of) any bill with this tag until
the deadline (`tax_rise`): kept at the deadline unless broken.
A press statement.

A town hall in the neighbourhood cast in `role`; with
`constituency`, one in every neighbourhood of the constituency.

A canvass of the neighbourhood cast in `role` (`or_town_hall`: a town
hall there counts too).

Be at a place of one of these kinds in the town (the first such
place; in the neighbourhood cast in `role`, if it has one).

A conversation with the person cast in `role`: the ask's own choice
in it (`choice`; a talk hook, S4), met when they agree.
Introduce a bill of these templates.

A bill of these templates becomes law (`sponsor_player`: the player's
own). A promise counts a failed vote on the player's own bill as
half kept (void: no cost, no reward).
"Sort it out" at the town hall (`Action::Casework`).

A fault on the streets where the neighbourhood (or the person, by
their home) cast in `role` is repaired (DEC-114, upkeep): cast on the
oldest open fault there that no other ask is about, met whoever
fixes it. "Sort it out" moves it up the repair queue.

None of the player's own hidden facts comes to light before the
deadline: kept at the deadline unless broken.

The player does not leak about the person cast in `role` (or tip
the press, E9) before the deadline: kept at the deadline unless broken.
As the player's party expects on the bill.

NeedsDef.description: A tier or competence a family or option needs (DEC-092 §5; M7).

NeighborhoodLean.description: A value per neighbourhood kind (omitted kinds are 0).

NominationGate.description: A party's conditions for nominating the player for a post (DEC-098).

min_standing.description: The player's Standing with the party must be at least this.

NpcParams.description: NPC AI balance numbers (DEC-030). Scores and curves are in `politics.ai`.

bill_interval_days.description: At most one bill of one's own in this many days.

bill_sunset_years.description: NPC bills sunset after this many years, [min, max].

busy_pending.description: The council is busy at this many pending bills, or this many laws in force.

close_margin.description: A race is a dead heat at 0 and not close at this poll margin.

crisis_agenda.description:
Agendas follow the town's character (DEC-077 §1): ranking its ideas, an
NPC adds this × severity to a template that answers the live crisis,
and `concern_agenda` × fit to one that addresses the town's concerns
(alignment with the concerns' attitudes, weighted by their levels).
The bonus changes which idea comes first, not how keen it is.

funds_in_ads.description: Funds count as full at this many ad buys.

ideologue_below.description:
Strategic profile from traits: an ideologue below this pragmatism,
else a populist above this ambition, else a pragmatist.

insurance_votes.description:
Whip counts: yes votes of insurance wanted beyond the threshold, the
gap at which a count stops being close, and the weight of a count
already on the right side.

lobby_closeness_keep.description:
Planning within a turn: closeness kept after lobbying, and the unknown
share kept after a contact.

two_ads_above.description:
Ads: two buys above this ad score, one above this, and the reserve
(in ad costs) a candidate keeps.

OccupationDef.description:
An occupation or role of Named characters (DEC-018): shopkeepers,
organisers, journalists, clergy, union stewards. Registry order is load order.

ambient.description: Passers-by (Ambient people) may have this occupation.

chance.description: Chance that one such person is generated per place (or neighbourhood).

class.description: Weights of the income classes they come from: [low, middle, high].

expertise.description: The issue they know best (an attitude key); random when omitted.

influence.description: How much weight a leader carries in town (0..1; power broker choice).

leader.description:
Organisation leaders (stewards, editors, chairs) are Principal
characters and can be a town's power broker.

places.description:
Place kinds where they work and can be met (or `streets`, one per
neighbourhood).

round.description:
Seeding round: a town's people of later rounds are generated after
everyone of earlier rounds, so occupations added later append to the
cast instead of renumbering it (draws are keyed by place and
occupation either way).

OccupationStake.description:
What an occupation has a stake in: the power broker of a town is the
leader with the biggest stake in its defining industry or live crisis.

crises.description: Crisis kinds (content ids) the occupation is drawn into.

drivers.description: Sector drivers (`industrial`, `extraction`, …) the occupation speaks for.

OfficeDef.description:
A single-holder office (DEC-017). Its id is also its role word (`mayor`):
Fluent `role-<id>`, and the word content uses.

calendar.description:
Its own election calendar (an office elected off the tier's cycle);
default: the tier's.

id.description: Unique across the constitution's tiers; at most [`PostKey::MAX`] bytes.

works_at.description: Where the holder works: a place kind (`places.jsonc` `key`).

OnBehalf.description:
Who the asker speaks for. A party's ask is voiced by the person cast as
the asker (its chair), and remembered as the party's.

OpenParams.description:
The open question's rule: the first of `order` the person has, and has
not already said to the player this week.

OpenRange.description: An inclusive range; either end may be left open.

OpinionParams.description:
Monthly opinion dynamics (DEC-025): experienced conditions and reactions
to laws and bills move approval of the local government and the player.

experience.description: What residents experience, in approval units (tanh scale).

gov_approval_rate.description: Monthly pull of government approval toward its target.

law_reaction_weight.description: Weight of reactions to laws in government approval, beside experience.

local_concerns.description:
How a neighbourhood's own conditions turn its town's indicators into
its own concern levels.

player_approval_rate.description: Monthly pull of approval of the player toward reactions to their bills.

player_reaction_scale.description: Sharpness of reactions to the player's bills.

policy_reaction.description: Weight of a bill or law's anticipated reaction per unit of awareness.

aftermath_key.description: What happened and why, after the choice (with the cast as arguments).

default.description:
What happens when the deadline passes without an answer (exactly one
option per dilemma; usually the costly one).

OptionDef2.description: One arrangement of a part of the room.

OptionOutcome.description: What an option of a decision beat does to the run.

oneOf.description: The player never began before its day passed: an empty chair.

OutletDef.description:
An outlet template (DEC-034): generated per town, region, or nation when
play begins.

finances.description: Yearly budget (currency), drawn in [min, max]: capacity and digging.

interests.description: Concerns it cares about (extra interest in stories that touch them).

journalists.description: Occupations of its journalists (Named people at its home place).

lean_sd.description: Spread of its editorial lean around its audience's views (per issue).

name_key.description:
Fluent key of the outlet's name (`$outlet_place`: its home place's
name for a town outlet, its region's name for a regional one).

place.description: A town outlet's home place kind (DEC-079): towns without one have none.

reach.description: Share of the scope's adults it reaches (an audience weight of 1).

social.description: A social platform: high reach, low credibility, spreads rumours.

stories_per_week.description: Stories it runs a week at a typical budget.

oneOf.description: One per town with its home place (`place`).
One per region.
One for the nation.

OverheardDef.description:
One thing residents may be heard saying at a diner, market, or union hall
(the "overheard" service). Each week every such place draws a few lines
that hold for its neighbourhood: lines about the neighbourhood's top
concerns, and opinions and news grounded in facts. Registry order is
load order. Fluent arguments always include `$town` and `$hood`; each
condition adds its own (see `condition::Condition::provides`).

concern.description:
Heard only where this concern is among the neighbourhood's top three
(a concern id); the stronger the concern, the likelier the line.

teaches.description:
What hearing the line lets the player hear of (DEC-091): each subject
is raised to `heard`. Lines have no roles; a neighbourhood or a place
is where the line is heard.

weight.description: Relative chance among the lines that hold (default 1).

hidden.description:
Not a slider: a value an option fixes for its mechanisms (DEC-092
families). Hidden parameters are never shown or set by a draft.

unit_key.description: Fluent key for the unit label.

PartRef.description: A part id, or alternatives the seed picks between.

attached_by_age.description: Share of adults attached to any party, by age band (young → old).

governing_credit.description:
Credit or blame for the party running the town hall: attachment to it
scales by 1 + (approval − 0.5) × this.

mover_rate.description: Yearly pull of the mover share toward current evaluations.

sharpness.description: Sharpness of attachment by ideological distance.

PartyLineParams.description:
The party line: one rule for the player's whip and for NPC members
(DEC-030). `score` = `platform` × the bill's fit with the party's
platform (−1..1) + a term for who sponsors it; inside ±`free_band` the
vote is free.

free_band.description: A score inside ±this is a free vote.

npc_pull.description:
How hard a whipped NPC member is pulled: lean = this × score × the
member's loyalty factor.

own_sponsor.description:
Sponsor terms: a bill from the party's own member, from the party that
governs (holds the signing office), and from any other party.

platform.description: Weight of the bill's fit with the party's platform.

PartyNameParts.description: Words for generated party names: an attitude-led adjective plus a noun.

PartyRel.description: Which party a cast colleague belongs to, relative to the player.

PatchDef.description: A patch of floor: another surface, a rug or a dais.

PerceptionParams.description:
What coverage does to beliefs (DEC-034 perception, DEC-025: perceived
personal impact as shaped by media).

approval.description: Approval of the subject lost per story × weight × heat × exposure × credibility.

awareness.description: Name recognition per story × exposure (a scandal makes you known).

framing.description: Hostile framing scales the hit by (1 + this × hostility).

legal_story.description: A legal development's story: × this (charges, a conviction), and an acquittal gives back this.

standing.description: The subject's Standing (party) per breaking scandal × weight.

statement.description: Approval per covered statement × framing × exposure × credibility.

valence.description: A politician's scandal valence (0..1) per story × weight × heat × exposure × credibility.

PersonFallback.description: Who a person slot binds when nobody matches (never an office name, DEC-098).

oneOf.description: The town's power broker.
Whoever holds the jurisdiction's executive office.

PersonalityAiParams.description:
Personality in opinion changes (DEC-031): the same rules for the player
and NPCs. (Loyalty in votes is `council.loyalty_discipline`; integrity
against lobbying is `council.lobby.integrity`.)

warmth_opinion.description: Opinion gains × (1 + w × (2 × warmth − 1)) of the holder.

oneOf.description: A campaign for one of its posts is running.
No campaign is running.

Pick.description: How a slot chooses among candidates.

oneOf.description: The lowest id: stable and plain.
Places: the largest job decline in their sector (E1 baselines).
Neighbourhoods and hazards: the highest exposure.
Neighbourhoods: the highest level of `concern`.
The most residents (neighbourhoods) or jobs (places).
A keyed draw among candidates.

PieceDef.description:
One placed part: on floor tiles, or on the back wall (a column and a
height `wy`, or standing on the floor line), or over the entrance (`front`).

chance.description: Present with this chance (0..1), keyed by the seed.

PitchParams.description: Pitching a bill (the shared lobbying formula and odds).

sway_share.description:
The share of a lobbying meeting's sway a pitch gives (a pitch costs
half the time).

PlaceArt.description: A place's art keys: an optional kit and the required family.

PlaceKindDef.description:
One kind of place and what it offers (DEC-079). Worldgen decides which
places exist; this registry supplies their behaviour.

actions.description: Actions offered here (keys from the action list).

addresses.description:
The concerns its service addresses (concern ids): its real need is
its neighbourhood's felt level of them (DEC-092 §2.22), what a
verb's `service` grant reads.

drivers.description:
The sector drivers of this kind of place (DEC-092 families: a plant's
sector, `drivers` selectors): the factory and the mill are
`industrial`, the mine `extraction`.

fallback.description:
Where this kind's actions and services move in a town (or, for
neighbourhood actions, a neighbourhood) that has no such place.

gateway.description: The gateway this kind of place is (DEC-110): where trade passes.

interior.description:
The interior recipe the player walks into (DEC-088; `interiors.jsonc`
id), presentation data like `layout`. A kind without one keeps the
place panel.

key.description:
Snake-case place kind, as worldgen names it (e.g. `council_chamber`),
or a pseudo-location (`home`, `streets`).

late_night.description: Actions that may also be taken here late at night (a subset of `actions`).

layout.description:
How the town layout draws it (DEC-090 D4, TOWN_GENERATION.md §6.3):
presentation data, validated but never read by the simulation.

sector.description:
The industry this kind of place is part of (a sector id): what a
verb's `sector` grant and its risk's `shedding` read.

verbs.description:
Verbs of the `visit` action offered here (`actions.jsonc`
`visit.verbs` ids; places with purpose, DEC-079 note).

footprint.description: `[[min w, min h], [max w, max h]]`, tiles (2..16); the largest is tried first.

place.description: Placement predicates in order of preference.

PlantOpens.description: How a plant of an industry comes back after one has closed.

oneOf.description:
Idle labour gathers in the town's investment pool; a works reopens
when the pool is a plant's size.
A long boom in the industry's demand reopens the works.
Never.

PlantState.description: A named plant's state in its review (DEC-110, `INDUSTRIES.md` §3).

oneOf.description: Working full time.
On short time.
Under notice, with a date.
Shut.

closes.description: Whether its plants close (false: they go on short time and stay).

founded.description: Age in years of a plant standing as history begins, [least, most].

margin_sd.description: Standard deviation of a plant's fixed margin.

named_share.description:
Share of the industry's capacity in a town its named plant takes,
[least, most]: one keyed draw.

place_kind.description:
The place kind (its `key`) that hosts this industry's plant; none:
the industry is small firms and crews only.

PlayerEventKey.description: Events about the player an ending can read.

oneOf.description: The party would not renominate them.
A sentence removed them from office.

axes.description: The design choices (1–3 axes of 2–3 options).

category.description: The budget line it is paid from.

max_instances.description: How many can be open at once in one jurisdiction.

name_key.description: Fluent keys for its title and summary; slot names are arguments.

needs.description: A power or competence the jurisdiction may lack (M7; shown, not used).

requires.description: The constitution power needed to propose it (never an office name).

slots.description:
What it is about, bound in order (a later slot may refer to an
earlier one).

tier.description: The tier of government whose jurisdictions it opens in (DEC-098).

trigger.description: When it comes onto the table; without one, as soon as its slots bind.

retired.description:
Retired (DEC-092 §2.19): not offered and not draftable by anyone;
bills and laws already made continue and saves that have them load.

secondary_backing.description:
What backs each secondary line (audit fix 8): a mechanism or side
effect of this template by its type (`rent_cap`, `grievance`), `cost`
(its money), or `measured:<metric>` (a side effect the audit measures
on twins, `SECONDARY_MEASURED`). Validation requires one for every
key, so a claim with nothing behind it cannot return unnoticed.

secondary_keys.description: Fluent keys for at least one secondary effect (REQ-006).

side_effects.description: Simulated downsides (DEC-073): every policy costs something besides money.

signature.description:
Value alignment by attitude key (DEC-025 anticipated channel, DEC-075).
Attitudes left out weigh 0.

unlock.description:
A situational policy (DEC-077 §3): on the table (offered, and
draftable by the player or an NPC) only while this trigger holds in
the town. A bill already drafted or a law already passed stays.
Always available without one.

party_count.description: Parties generated per world under plurality rules (two majors plus minors).

party_line.description: How a party takes a position on a bill (the party line, DEC-027).

early_multiplier.description: Shared error multiplier at the start of the campaign.

shared_sd.description: Election-wide shared error on election eve (share, 0..1 scale).

PrepDef.description: A mark from an earlier beat that adds a line or removes a risk (§3.4).

adds.description: A kind of line the mark gives (`second`, `proof`).

bars.description: Sources the other side keeps off while the mark is set.

evidence.description: For `adds: proof`: the evidence what was found carries (0..1).

oneOf.description: The first round is not cold: the player knew what was coming.

contact.description: Campaign contact scale (everywhere in the race), unless there was a gaffe.

gaffe_approval.description: Approval lost to a gaffe, per unit of awareness.

PriceDef.description: What adopting a sponsor's version costs the player.

oneOf.description: Favours owed to the sponsor (DEC-031); they call them in later.

A public endorsement: approval rises among the sponsor's people
(`classes`, or the residents of `area`) and falls a little elsewhere.

deliberation_days.description: Days between introduction and the first stage (deliberation).

ProductDef.description:
What a town's branch of an industry makes (DEC-110): text and siting
only; nothing is simulated per product.

good.description: The good it is (a good id): what a tariff or a trade deal names.

product_key.description: Fluent key of the product as a mass noun ("canned fish").

with.description: The industry whose presence nearby picks this product.

works_key.description: Fluent key of the works' noun ("cannery").

PromiseAnswers.description: What a promise answers (validation: every promise names it).

oneOf.description:
The town's live crisis: the menu offers each template that answers it
(the `answer` argument). Offered only while a crisis is live.
A worry of the constituency's voters.
No one worry (a promise of presence, of honesty).
The end of the term of the post the player is running for.
The end of the first full budget year after election day.
This many days after election day.

broken_discount.description: × this per public promise the player has broken.

persuasion.description:
Persuasion a promise adds where its worry is felt: × the felt level
of the worry in each neighbourhood of the race (× `any_salience` for
a promise that answers no worry), approval × room.

ProxyParams.description:
The player-proxy's numbers (DEC-012). It is kept modest on purpose: a
skip is a convenience, never the best way to play (DEC-097).

answers.description:
Decision weights the proxy answers; others it leaves to the player
(or to their default at the deadline).

idle_share.description: The share of slots it leaves unused (a proxy is not the player).

learns.description:
Whether what the proxy's acts would teach is kept (DEC-102 clause 7:
a skip learns nothing new, so `false`). With `true` a skipped
canvass fills the notebook as the player's own would.

max_commands.description: At most this many commands a turn.

RaiseDef.description:
When a fault opens: each month, in each neighbourhood whose condition is
below `below`, with the chance `chance × (below − condition) / below`,
× `winter` in December, January and February.

below.description: Condition (0–1) below which it can open.

chance.description: The monthly chance at a condition of 0 (0–1).

RaisedBy.description:
What raises a decision other than the director's spotlight: a story
about the player, or an investigation of them. Raised decisions are
fairness first (DEC-006): never budgeted.

ask_kept.description:
Delivery (ENGAGEMENT §2.2): an ask kept, a campaign promise kept and
an ask broken (negative), read by the asks domain (E6); the player's
own bill becoming law, credited with V1.

RelevanceWeights.description: Relevance scoring (DEC-033): what connects a situation to the player.

arc.description: A beat of a running arc.

concern.description: It answers one of the town's top concerns.

crisis.description: × the live crisis's severity, when the situation answers to it.

election.description: The player's seat is up within a year.

memory.description: Per salient memory a cast person holds of the player (up to three).

player.description: A cast person has history with the player (an edge, a favour).

pressure.description: It reads one of the player's pressure tracks.

ward.description: The situation is in the player's ward.

RepairDef.description:
What a repair costs (money at the starting price level; the engine
scales it by prices) and how long it takes once paid for.

ResourceStock.description: A regional resource stock an industry draws on.

ResponseParams.description: Responses to a story (the player's and NPCs').

ad_heat.description: An ad buy during a scandal keeps this much heat (changing the subject).

apologise_evidence.description: An apology is an admission: prosecutors' evidence rises by this.

counter_hostility.description: A counter-attack turns the outlet that broke it more hostile.

deny_heat.description: Heat kept after a denial when the evidence is weak (below `deny_strong`).

deny_strong.description: Evidence at which a denial unravels: heat × `deny_backfire_heat` and Standing.

statement_heat.description: A covered statement during a scandal keeps this much heat (× sympathy).

RiderKind.description: A rider a decision can attach to a bill.

oneOf.description: A project in the player's ward (costs the town money).
The law expires after four years.

id.description:
Role id, referenced by conditions, effects, and Fluent arguments
(`<id>` is the person's name, `<id>-role` their role key).

RoleGroupDef.description:
A group of roles whose informative lines are written from one vantage
point (occupation ids and role words of the constitution's posts).

RoleRamps.description: The variable material roles' ramps, one picked per room by the seed.

RoundDef.description: One round: who speaks and the sources they may draw on, best first.

RoutineDay.description: A day of the week, as content writes it.

RoutineDef.description:
A routine: whom it is for, and its rules in order. Exactly one of
`post`, `occupation` and `role`.

post.description:
A post's role word from the constitution (a body's `member_key`, an
office's id).

role.description:
A special role. The broker's and the rival's routines come before
their post's or occupation's; `politician` and `anyone` after.

RoutineEvent.description: A routine event: `session`, `vote`, `campaign`, `meeting_night`, or a calendar event's id (`event.<name>`, held today in their town).

RoutineRole.description: Special roles a routine can be for.

oneOf.description: The town's power broker (DEC-077 §1).
The named rival of the town's leading figure.
A politician holding no post (a challenger, a former official).
Any stored character (the last routine tried).

RoutineRule.description: One rule of a routine: when it applies and where it sends them.

at.description:
Where they go, by weight (spots their town lacks are skipped; a rule
with none left does not apply).

chance.description:
Chance (0..1] the rule applies on a given day and part, keyed by the
person, the day and the part.

days.description: Weekdays of the day played this turn (none listed: all).

events.description: Events that must all be going on.

parts.description: Day parts it applies in (none listed: all).

unless.description: Events none of which may be going on.

RoutineSpot.description: Where a rule sends someone, with a weight.

correction_chance.description: Weekly chance a credible outlet corrects it (× its credibility).

correction_share.description: Share of the harm a correction undoes.

spread_weeks.description: Weeks a rumour spreads on social platforms.

weight.description: A rumour's weight beside a real scandal of the same severity.

ScandalResponseKind.description: How the player answers a story (DEC-034 player communication).

oneOf.description: Say nothing (the story runs its course).

ScenarioDef.description:
A starting world: biases on world generation (geography, economy, era,
politics). Everything left out is drawn at random, as for a random
country, so a scenario only says what makes it different.

name_key.description: Fluent key of the name shown on the title screen.

class_mix.description: Multipliers on each neighbourhood's income-class mix: `[low, middle, high]`.

endowment.description: Multiplies the structural presence of sectors with a driver (omitted = 1).

ScenarioEra.description: The trends of the age: technology and industry, and the climate's drift.

drying.description: Annual drying of the climate; random when omitted.

storminess.description: Annual growth in storminess; random when omitted.

country_extent.description: Size of the country within the map.

industrial_towns.description: Every town and city (not rural places) has an industrial district.

mountain_strength.description: Strength of mountain ranges (0..1); random when omitted.

population.description: Population multiplier on the world size's population.

sea_sides.description: Sides of the country on the sea (1–3); random when omitted.

temp_south.description: Mean temperature in the south (°C); random when omitted.

attitude_shift.description: Added to every cohort's seeded opinion, by attitude key (omitted = 0).

SceneDef.description: A scene template: a short exchange with a character at a place.

teaches.description:
What answering the decision this scene presents teaches (DEC-091),
with the dilemma's roles. The cast people are met (`known`) anyway.

oneOf.description: Where the person in `role` works, else a place of the `fallback` kind.

A place of this kind in town (`streets` = the streets of the cast
neighbourhood or the player's home neighbourhood).

Scope.description: Which voters an approval or awareness effect reaches.

oneOf.description: The player's ward.
The whole town.

Season.description: A season (months 12–2 are winter, 3–5 spring, 6–8 summer, 9–11 autumn).

base_wage.description: Mean annual wage per worker at price level 1.0 (currency units).

base_weight.description: Relative weight of this sector's base presence in a generic economy.

cyclicality.description: Elasticity of job demand to the global demand cycle.

driver.description: Which coded behaviour this sector follows.

talk_key.description:
Fluent key of the sector as residents name it in talk (a noun phrase
such as "the factories"); the name is used without one.

SectorDriver.description:
Behaviour driver of a sector (DEC-075): the closed set of economic
behaviours implemented in code. Sectors themselves are content; several
sectors may share a driver, and a new driver needs a code change.

oneOf.description: Farming and other land-based output: fertility, crop prices, water.
Mining, energy, timber: commodity prices and finite stocks; plant closures.
Manufacturing: national competitiveness and unit labour costs; plant closures.
Construction: housing starts and public spending.
Retail and local services: household consumption.
Tourism and hospitality: scenery, coasts, disasters.
Knowledge and technology: productivity follows the technology trend.
Public employment: funded by government spending.

SectorKindLean.description: Extra share of one sector driver's workers by neighbourhood kind.

ShadyActionDef.description: A shady action at a place (DEC-079): its payoff and the hidden fact it leaves.

SideEffectDef.description:
A simulated downside of a policy (DEC-073). The amount is `per_unit`
times the named parameter (or 1 without one), scaled by implementation
progress, funding, and pilot size like the mechanisms.

oneOf.description:
Disruption while the programme is being built (roadworks, construction):
lowers the town's appeal and residents' approval until complete.

A lasting grievance among a group the policy hurts materially (approval
of the government, and of the sponsor). Negative amounts are relief.

min_age_band.description: Only adults in this age band or older (0 = 18–29 … 3 = 65+).

oneOf.description: Changes how much a class works (share of its labour force).

Sides.description: The two sides of an arc, by role.

SidesDef.description: Who is across from the player, who may chair, who may speak for them.

chair.description: A person role that may ask a round's question.

second.description: A person role that may speak for the player (the `second` line).

SiteFlag.description: A yes-or-no fact about a town an industry's siting needs or likes.

oneOf.description: The town is on a river.
A rail link reaches the town.
The town has an industrial district.

SitingDef.description:
Where an industry settles (DEC-110): a town's score is
`(base + Σ geo weights × the town's geography) × likes × by_class × near
× the region's tradition × a town draw`, and zero when a `needs` flag
fails.

by_class.description: Multiplier by settlement class: rural, town, city, metro.

gateways.description: Multipliers for gateways a town has.

likes.description: Multipliers for flags a town has.

near.description: Multipliers where another industry is strong in the town.

needs_gateway.description: Gateways a town must have (a port for a shipyard).

regional_sd.description:
Standard deviation (in logs) of each region's tradition: one keyed
draw per region and industry.

SituationTrigger.description:
A trigger on a jurisdiction's situation: it holds while every `all`
condition holds and, when any are given, one of the `any` conditions
does. Situational policies' unlocks and policy families' triggers and
expiry (DEC-092).

any.description:
At least one of these holds, when any are given (the one condition
language, `condition.rs`).

reason_key.description: Fluent key naming the circumstances, e.g. `unlock-closure`.

SizeParams.description: An attack's size, by source, where it is not read from state.

absent.description: A beat never taken, a decision let pass (each).

failed_line.description: A law whose ledger delivers less than this is "failed".

governing_line.description: The government's approval under which its record is an attack.

gravity_ethics.description: How grave a hidden fact is, by its severity.

lean_line.description: How far a group must lean against a vote before it is an attack.

question.description: The room's question: not an attack.

recency_days.description: Days over which a broken promise fades to half.

thin_line.description: The record under which "thin" is an attack.

SkipTargetKind.description: A point a skip can run to (an engine contract).

oneOf.description: The start of the next chapter (a new session, or the campaign).
The opening of the campaign for the player's post.
Election day for the player's post.
The end of the player's term.

SlotDef.description: One slot: what it binds and whether a family can open without it.

SourceKind.description:
Where a prompt comes from (§4.1): code that reads one owner's state and
gives zero or more true things to put to the player.

preset.description: One option per axis (a missing axis: its default).

slot.description: The person slot of whoever sponsors it.

SpotDef.description: Where a person present stands or sits, by role.

SpotDef2.description: A fault's spot kind and how many such spots a neighbourhood has.

slots.description: Spots of this kind on a neighbourhood's streets (1–16).

SpotKind.description:
Where on a neighbourhood's streets a fault is (the client maps a kind
and a slot to a cell of the street).

oneOf.description: The carriageway: potholes, a sunken manhole.
The pavement and what stands on it: lamps, signs, bins.
The kerb and the gutter: drains.
A bus stop or a shelter.
A green, a play area, a bench.
A vote of a body under a decision rule.
An office signs or vetoes; a veto may be overridden by a body.

climax.description:
The turn: the chapter's climax when this arc leads. A run records
the first turn it reaches (`ArcRun::turn`).

clock.description: A deadline set on entry; later stages keep it until one sets another.

hidden.description: Not shown until the ledger says so (task A3).

key.description:
The story so far (an exit's: how it ended), with the cast and the
arc's facts as arguments.

next.description:
Edges in priority order, checked weekly and on entry: the first
that holds is taken.

rise.description: Heat added each week the stage lasts.

Standing.description: The kind of chapter a standing arc gives its turn to.

oneOf.description: A budget year in office (the budget round).
The player's campaign (the rival).

StartProfile.description: What a background knows when play begins (DEC-091).

StatementDef.description: What a statement must be about.

oneOf.description:
The town's live crisis: a general statement while it lasts, or one on
a bill that answers it.
A worry: a general statement, or one on a bill that answers it.
The bill cast in `role`.
Any statement.

StatusKey.description: A run status an ending can read.

StockExposure.description: A stock an industry depends on: demand scales with `stock ^ power`.

StorytellerDef.description:
A storyteller profile (DEC-033 addendum): a transparent difficulty and
flavour lever over chance and pacing, never over consequences.

budget_scale.description: Multiplies the significant and minor budgets.

build_up_scale.description: Scales build-up and relax lengths: frequency, not amplitude.

cycle.description:
Pace each chapter in build-up, peak and relax phases (ENGAGEMENT
§4.3); off, situations come by chance within the budgets.

defer_hazards.description:
Hold hazards in the player's town while it carries `crisis_cap`
crises. Timing only: a held hazard still strikes, at its drawn severity.

hazard_rate.description:
Share of hazard strikes in the player's town that happen (1 = the
hazard model as drawn).

hold_recessions.description: Hold the onset of a global recession while the player's town is at the cap.

tension_curve.description:
Pace decisions along the chapter's tension curve (otherwise spotlight
whatever is ready, within the budgets).

SubjectDef.description:
A knowledge subject named by role, never by id (DEC-091;
M6_ENGINE_CONTRACTS §1.3): resolved against the cast and the player's
town by `mandate_sim::narrative::learn`. Used by narrative `learn`
effects, scene `teaches` hooks, `knows` conditions, and overheard lines'
`teaches` (which have no roles: there, the neighbourhood is where the
line is heard).

oneOf.description: The player's town's worries.

A neighbourhood's worries: the neighbourhood cast in `role`, or the
home neighbourhood of the person cast in it; without a role, where it
happens (where an overheard line is heard; a decision's scene, else
the player's home neighbourhood).
Who really runs the player's town.
The person cast in `role`.
The rival's plans.
Who supports a policy: the bill or law cast in `role`, or a template.

A situational policy on the table (transitional, until the M5d
templates become policy families).

Places of these kinds (any kind if empty) in the player's town: in
the neighbourhood cast in `role` (or the home neighbourhood of the
person cast in it), else where it happens. Hidden places (DEC-090 D7)
use this; ordinary places are always known.

SubjectRef.description: A subject of the player's ledger, named from the conversation.

oneOf.description:
The town's worries: `$concern_key` (the strongest; its noun phrase
of talk, `$concern_talk_key`).
A neighbourhood's worries: `$hood`, `$concern_key`, `$concern_talk_key`.
Who really runs the town: `$broker`, `$broker_place`, `$stake_key`.
A person in a slot (`speaker`, `about`): `$person`.
The rival's plans: `$rival`.

A proposal sponsored by a person in a slot (DEC-092; holds nothing
until policy families exist).
Who supports the policy in a slot (`about`): `$policy_key`, `$support_key`.

SupportParams.description: Asking for support or a public endorsement.

base.description:
Odds for a non-politician: sigmoid(base + opinion × per_opinion / 100
+ (trust − 0.5) × per_trust), clamped to [min, max].

bill_awareness.description: Backing a bill in public raises its awareness by this much.

endorse_approval.description:
A public endorsement: approval of the player among the residents of
the endorser's neighbourhood (× the room left).

favour_below.description: Below this opinion, someone who agrees asks a favour in return.

sway.description: A politician who agrees backs the bill: this much sway.

SurfaceRef.description: A surface of the art pack and its ramps (a second ramp for two-colour surfaces).

ramps.description: Ramp references: a palette ramp (`stone`, `grass+1`) or a material role (`@wood`).

TableDef.description:
Offers wait on the table and take effect only if a deal is struck
(§2.4). **Not built yet** (the negotiation arrives with the favour's
arc): parsed and validated, and an arc that uses it is never raised.

TableWant.description: Something the other side asks for across a table.

oneOf.description: The player's vote on the bill cast in a role.

TalkChoiceDef.description:
The choice a talk need puts in the conversation with its person (a talk
hook, S4): the button (`label_key`), what the player says (`say_key`),
and the replies, the first whose conditions hold (slots `speaker` and
`player`) being said. A reply that `agrees` meets the need; one that
does not leaves it open, and the ask says so. The last reply has no
conditions, so there is always one. Arguments: the ask's people by role
(`$asker`, `$official`, …), a bill role as `$<role>_key` (`$bill` in the
text), and `$speaker`, `$player`, `$town`.

TalkCost.description: What a conversation costs (DEC-073; owner, 2026-11-19: half a slot).

oneOf.description: Two conversations fill one slot.

TalkEffectDef.description: A change to the relationship a line makes (the speaker toward the player).

oneOf.description: Opinion change, scaled by the speaker's personality.
A memory of the player (a memory kind).

TalkLeadDef.description: A lead a line opens (a deflecting line usually points somewhere).

subject.description: The subject following the lead teaches, and to what level.

TalkLineDef.description:
One reply line: a Fluent key, the conditions under which it may be said,
and what it teaches, where it points and how it moves the relationship.

fallback.description:
The topic's safe answer for the roles in its `occupation` condition
(or all roles); used only when no other substance line holds.

lead.description: Where the line points the player.

miss.description:
The line says the speaker does not know (or cannot say): on a topic
that informs, a reply whose substance it is costs no time
(`talk_params.miss_free`). Every fallback line is a miss; this marks
the others ("Not my end of town"). A miss teaches nothing.

teaches.description: What the player learns, each capped at the speaker's told level.

topic.description:
The topic a substance line answers (required for substance; an
opener with a topic is preferred for that topic).

voice.description: The voice a closer belongs to (required for closers).

weight.description: Relative chance among the lines that hold (default 1).

TalkMechanic.description: What a topic does besides the reply. A small closed set kept in code.

oneOf.description: Only the reply (and what it teaches).
Sway on a bill, by the shared lobbying formula.
Ask for support or a public endorsement (odds shown first).
Offer a favour, or call one in (the favour ledger).
A small opinion gain (capped weekly) and a `met` memory.

The open question ("What's on your mind?"): the engine chooses what
the person most wants to say from their own state (an ask of the
player, their main worry, gossip they hold; `talk_params.open`), and
the reply is about that. The player names no subject: the topic's
`about` kinds are what the engine may choose.

TalkParams.description: The conversation parameter block (`kind: "talk_params"`, once across packs).

favour_discretion.description: Added when a favour they owe the player is called in.

flattered_discretion.description: Added when flattered (after small talk with them this week): `trait.vain`: +1.

likely_from.description:
A subject counts as likely for a speaker when public facts say they
would know it at least this well (the talk panel lists those first).

log_cap.description: Exchanges kept in the log (the notebook's "where and when").

memory_lines.description: Lines remembered per person for the repetition guard.

miss_free.description:
A miss costs no time: a question on a topic that informs, answered
only by the topic's safe answer (the person does not know, or will
not say), is not charged.

open.description: The open question ("What's on your mind?").

quote_share.description: How often a memory quote is used when one holds (0..1).

role_groups.description:
The role groups informative lines are written for (the doctor's
coverage check reads them; every role belongs to one).

small_talk_opinion.description: Small talk's opinion gain (scaled by personality).

small_talk_weekly_cap.description: Small talks per person per week that still gain anything.

trait_discretion.description: Whole levels added to the cap by traits (`trait.schemer`: −1).

TalkPart.description: Which part of a reply a line is, in reply order.

income.description: Effective income tax by class: low, middle, high (national tier).

property.description: Annual property tax as a share of dwelling value (local tier).

TeachDef.description:
A scene's teaching hook: what answering the decision it presents lets
the player learn (DEC-091).

TeachDef2.description: One thing a line teaches, capped at the speaker's told level.

TemperDef.description: A room's anger scales every gain down; some lines cool it (§2.4).

TemperParams.description: A room's temper (§2.4): what cools it.

oneOf.description: The run's own heat.

TemptationParams.description: NPCs' temptations (DEC-030: the same acts and the same exposure).

acts.description: What they take: the player's diner bribe, or a donor deal.

chance.description: Chance per turn for an officeholder of integrity 0 (× ambition factor).

TensionParams.description:
The chapter's tension curve: it rises from `start` to `peak` at `peak_at`
(a share of the chapter), then falls to `end`.

catch_up_at.description: From this share of a chapter on, a chapter short of its minimum spotlights whatever is ready.

climax_window.description: The share of a session chapter in which its climax may come, [from, to].

crisis_weight.description: Weights of live tension: the town's worst crisis, pending decisions, the player's race, and track danger.

slack.description: A significant decision is spotlighted while tension is below the curve plus this.

TerrainFeatureDef.description:
A terrain feature (§6.1): its generator, when it applies, the generator's
integer parameters, and art keys.

params.description:
The generator's parameters: integers (per mille where a share), lists
and tables of integers, or flags. The generator is integer-only.

TerrainGenerator.description: The code that draws a terrain feature (an extension point, §6.5).

elections.description:
When this tier's elections happen (its elected bodies and offices,
unless one has its own `calendar`).

TopicDef.description: Something the player can raise with someone (DEC-093).

about.description: Which subjects it can be about (empty: none).

about_required.description: The topic needs a subject (a pitch needs a bill); otherwise one is optional.

name_key.description: Fluent key of the button label.

TopicOffer.description: Who offers a topic, where, and when.

places.description: Place kinds (`streets` for a neighbourhood's streets); empty: anywhere.

broker_seniority.description:
Power broker: weight of an officeholder's seniority (per year in
office) against a leader's influence and stake.

broker_stake.description:
Stake weight of a leader whose stake matches the defining industry
or the live crisis.

trend_months.description: Months of crisis severity kept for the trend.

TownDistrictDef.description:
A district type (§6.2): when the generator may choose it for a
neighbourhood, how its streets, plots and buildings are laid out, and its
art keys.

bill_nudge.description:
Approval nudge per unit of alignment with the bill discussed, and
without a bill.

contact_base.description:
Campaign contact: (`contact_base` + `contact_oratory` × oratory), ×
`hostile_contact` when hostile. NPC town halls use the same scale.

hostile_nudge.description: Approval nudge from a hostile crowd.

risk_base.description:
Chance of a hostile crowd: `risk_base` − `risk_approval` × the
player's net approval − `risk_government` × (government approval −
0.5), within [`risk_min`, `risk_max`].

TownLayerFilter.description:
A way to narrow a markers layer. The engine says which markers each
filter keeps; the client only hides the rest.

oneOf.description: The members of the home legislature (named by the constitution).
One filter per party that has someone on the layer.
People the player knows (met or seen), not only heard of.

TownLayerKind.description: How a layer is drawn over the town.

oneOf.description:
Outlines of areas made of neighbourhoods, each labelled, with a
marker for whoever holds it.
People or things at places, clustered where they would overlap.

Every neighbourhood filled by its class of a figure; an unknown
